web|title=Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Survivor – NDS – Review |url=http://nds.gamezone.com/reviews/item/shin_megami_tensei_devil_survivor_nds_review/ |publisher=GameZone |access-date=15 May 2011 |date=22 June 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110812012841/http://nds.gamezone.com/reviews/item/shin_megami_tensei_devil_survivor_nds_review |archive-date=12 August 2011}}</ref> as well as an innovative demon auction system and a death clock system where each character has a specified time of death<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ds.ign.com/objects/142/14294464.html |title=IGN: SMT: Devil Survivor review, IGN|website=IGN |access-date=18 May 2010}}</ref> and the player's actions has consequences on who lives and dies.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siliconera.com/2009/05/27/devil-survivor-and-the-countdown-clock-to-death/|title=Devil Survivor and the Countdown Clock To Death|publisher=Siliconera|author=Spencer|date=27 May 2009|access-date=16 May 2011}}</ref> On the [[PlayStation Portable]] (PSP), ''[[Half-Minute Hero]]'' (2009) is a [[Role-playing shooters|role-playing shooter]] featuring self-referential humour and a 30-second time limit for each level and boss encounter.<ref>{{cite web|title=2D Forever: the fall and rise of hardcore Japanese game design|work=[[The Guardian]]|last=Stuart |first=Keith |date=4 March 2011|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/gamesblog/2011/mar/04/2d-forever-japanese-game-design|access-date=23 March 2011}}</ref> ''[[Infinite Space]]'' (2009) by [[PlatinumGames]] is a hybrid of [[tactical role-playing game]], [[real-time strategy]] and [[Space flight simulator game|space simulator]] elements,<ref name="n-europe_space">{{cite web|url=http://n-europe.com/news.php?nid=13865 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110714145320/http://n-europe.com/news.php?nid=13865 |url-status=dead |archive-date=14 July 2011 |publisher=N-Europe |title=News: Infinite Space Dated For and an epic scale spanning hundreds of planets.<ref>{{cite web|last=Castle|first=Matthew|title=Infinite Space|url=http://www.gamesradar.com/infinite-space/|publisher=[[GamesRadar]]|access-date=2 May ====Aftermath (early 2010s)====
In the early 2010s, new intellectual properties such as ''[[Xenoblade Chronicles (video game)|Xenoblade Chronicles]]'' from [[Monolith Soft]] and ''[[The Last Story]]'' from [[Mistwalker]] found a home on Nintendo's [[Wii]] console late in its lifespan, gaining unanimously solid reviews. Many reviewers claimed the games revitalized the genre, keeping its best traits while modernizing other gameplay elements which could appeal to a wide audience. ''Xenoblade'', in particular, revitalized the genre with an extremely expansive [[open world]]. However, [[Nintendo of America]] announced its decision to not localize the games, not having enough faith in their commercial appeal to American audiences. In response, a widespread internet campaign known as "[[Operation Rainfall]]" petitioned the release of ''Xenoblade'', ''The Last Story'', and ''[[Pandora's Tower]]'' in America, with participants flooding Nintendo's official Facebook page with requests and sending mail to NOA's headquarters. The former two games were released in America in 2012, with ''Xenoblade'' debuting at the top of [[GameStop]]'s best seller list the week of its release. Despite this, the sales of both games were far less than those of console WRPGs such as
''[[Mass Effect 2]]'' and ''Fallout 3''.

On handhelds, the 2010 Atlus title ''[[Radiant Historia]]'' introduced a unique take on the concept of [[Nonlinear gameplay|non-linear]] branching storylines that gives the player the freedom to alter the course of history through time travel across two parallel timelines.<ref name="1UP_Radiant_Historia">{{cite web|last=Parish |first=Jeremy |title=Radiant Historia Gives Off a Distinct Chrono Trigger Vibe |url=http://www.1up.com/previews/radiant-historia-distinct-chrono-trigger |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121210102047/http://www.1up.com/previews/radiant-historia-distinct-chrono-trigger |url-status=dead |archive-date=10 December 2012 |website=[[1UP.com]] |access-date=15 May 2011 |date=11 November 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=North|first=Dale|title=Review: Radiant ''[[Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together|Tactics Ogre]]'' features a similar "World" system that allows players to revisit key plot points and make different choices to see how the story unfolds [[Imageepoch]]'s 2011 title ''Saigo no Yakusoku no Monogatari'' (''Final Promise Story'') for the PSP has a strategic command-based battle system where enemies learn from previous skirmishes and where In 2011, Nintendo made a conscious effort to revitalize the Pokémon brand with the [[Pokémon Black and White|''Pokémon Black'' & ''White'']] duology, which streamlined the battle system and introduced an entirely new lineup of characters in a new region based on New York City. These games were followed up with a [[Pokémon Black 2 and White 2|direct numbered sequel]] in 2012, a first for the main series. 2012 also saw the release of ''[[Pokémon Conquest]]'', a crossover with the ''[[Nobunaga's Ambition]]'' series of strategy role-playing games.<ref name="releasedate">{{cite news |url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/interest/2011-12-16/pokemon+nobunaga-ambition-game-revealed |title=Pokémon + Nobunaga's Ambition Game Revealed |work=[[Anime News Network]] |date=16 December 2011}}</ref>

In 2012 and onwards, a surge in new JRPGs such as ''[[Xenoblade Chronicles (video game)|Xenoblade Chronicles]]'', ''[[Persona 4 Golden]]'', ''[[Fire Emblem Awakening]]'', ''[[Shin Megami Tensei 4]]'', ''[[Tales of Graces]]'', ''[[Kingdom Hearts 3D: Dream Drop Distance]]'', ''[[Etrian Odyssey IV: Legends of the Titan]]'', ''[[Ni no Kuni: Wrath of the White Witch]]'' and ''[[Tales of Xillia]]'' are generally well received by fans of the genre and some critics while a number of popular WRPGs such as ''[[Mass Effect 3]]'' and the PC version of ''[[Diablo III]]'' suffered from poor feedback by non-critic reviewers, especially on [[Metacritic]]. JRPG installments from mainstream franchises such as ''[[Paper Mario: Sticker Star]]'' performed well below expectations, continuing the decline of mainstream JRPG franchises except Pokémon. With the exception of Pokémon games, individual JRPG sales continue to pale in comparison against individual WRPGs such as ''[[The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-12-16-valve-skyrim-fastest-selling-game-in-steam-history|title=Valve: Skyrim fastest-selling game in Steam history • News • Eurogamer.net|date=16 December 2011|access-date=16 December 2011|website=Eurogamer}}</ref> and ''[[Guild Wars 2]]''.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Matt|first=Peckham|title=Guild Wars 2 nabs fastest selling MMO crown|url=https://techland.time.com/2013/08/16/guild-wars-2-nabs-fastest-selling-western-mmo-crown-looks-east-for-more-records/|journal= [[Time Inc.|Time]]|access-date=21 October 2013|date=16 August 2013}}</ref> However, JRPGs released by Nintendo continue to prosper, with ''[[Dragon Quest IX]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.siliconera.com/2011/01/27/heres-how-much-dragon-quest-ix-sold-overseas/|title=Here's How Much Dragon Quest IX Sold Overseas|date=27 January 2011}}</ref> ''[[Fire Emblem Awakening]]'', and ''[[Bravely Default]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/bravely-defaults-strong-sales-continue-reach-1-mil/1100-6421345/|title=Bravely Default's Strong Sales Continue, Reach 1 Million Worldwide|first=Chris|last=Pereira|date=29 July 2014}}</ref> selling well above expectations for the genre, and ''[[Final Fantasy XIV]]'' has reported such a strong revenue that Square Enix, its publisher, had expected turning a profit,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2014/02/05/square-enix-financials-cast-final-fantasy-14-as-saviour|title=Square Enix Financials Cast Final Fantasy 14 as Saviour|first=Luke|last=Karmali|date=5 February 2014}}</ref> so while certain games may still be ill-received, others are performing fairly well.

====New directions and renaissance (2010s–present)====
Hunting RPGs are a type of action RPG subgenre featuring the player and an optional team of up to three other players hunting down larger monsters with a set amount of time, using weapons crafted from the materials extracted from the map and/or from the monsters themselves. Unlike most RPG genres, the monsters have no health bars or hit points, but have stronger attack and defense stats, forcing the players to use survival items and coordinated strategies to eliminate a specific monster. First appeared in [[Capcom]]'s ''[[Monster Hunter]]'' franchise, these games later expanded the hunting RPG genre into other games as well, such as [[Bandai Namco Entertainment]]'s ''[[God Eater (series)|God Eater]]'' franchise.

[[Soulslike]] games are a relatively new genre born due to popularity of the ''[[Dark Souls]]'' series.<ref>{{cite web|last=Byrd |first=Matthew |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/games/how-dark-souls-became-its-own-genre/ |title=How Dark Souls Became Its Own Genre |publisher=Den of Geek |date=2 May 2016 |access-date=7 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://geektyrant.com/news/5-games-series-that-have-defined-a-genre |title=5 Games Series That Have Defined a Genre – GeekTyrant |date=9 July 2015 |publisher=Geektyrant.com |access-date=7 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://whatculture.com/gaming/10-upcoming-souls-like-games-to-play-after-dark-souls-3 |title=10 Upcoming 'Souls Like' Games To Play After Dark Souls 3 |publisher=Whatculture.com |date=4 May 2016 |access-date=7 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cubedgamers.com/2017/01/27/nioh-naysayers-and-the-manifestation-of-the-soulslike/ |title=Nioh Naysayers and the Manifestation of the Soulslike |publisher=Cubed Gamers |date=27 January 2017 |access-date=7 March 2017 |archive-date=7 March 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307220917/http://www.cubedgamers.com/2017/01/27/nioh-naysayers-and-the-manifestation-of-the-soulslike/ |url-status=dead}}</ref> Those games generally have common elements like high difficulty, high-risk combat with hard-hitting enemies, sparse checkpoints, and enemies dropping souls (or some other resource used for upgrading stats and/or weapons that is lost upon death), but the player has one chance to regain the dropped souls if they can reach the place of their death without dying again.

Since 2016, Japanese RPGs have been experiencing a resurgence,<ref name="gamerevolution2016">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamerevolution.com/features/13902-2017-the-year-japanese-rpgs-caught-up-to-western-rpgs|title=2017: The Year Japanese RPGs Caught Up To Western RPGs|date=27 March 2017|website=GameRevolution}}</ref><ref name="usgamer2016">{{cite web|url=https://www.usgamer.net/articles/the-jrpg-is-doing-just-fine-thanks|title=The JRPG is Doing Just Fine, Thanks|first=Jeremy|last=Parish|date=21 December 2016|access-date=16 January 2019|archive-date=6 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181206145448/https://www.usgamer.net/articles/the-jrpg-is-doing-just-fine-thanks|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="technobuffalo2016">{{cite web|url=https://www.technobuffalo.com/2016/12/27/did-2016-truly-hold-up-as-a-comeback-year-for-the-jrpg-genre/|title=Did 2016 truly hold up as a comeback year for the JRPG genre?|date=27 December 2016}}</ref> as part of a renaissance for the Japanese video game industry.<ref name="verge2016">{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2017/6/30/15894404/japan-video-game-comeback-zelda-resident-evil-e3-2017|title=How Japanese video games made a comeback in 2017|first=Andrew|last=Webster|date=30 June 2017|website=The Verge}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Pinnell |first=James |url=https://www.pcauthority.com.au/feature/yakuza-nioh-and-the-new-japan-renaissance-453105 |title=PC & Tech Authority &#124; TechRadar |publisher=Pcauthority.com.au |date=11 September 2014 |access-date=8 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171026105505/https://www.pcauthority.com.au/feature/yakuza-nioh-and-the-new-japan-renaissance-453105 |archive-date=26 October 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2016, the global success of ''[[Pokémon Go]]'' helped ''[[Pokémon Sun and Moon]]'' set sales records around the world.<ref name="usgamer2016"/> ''[[Final Fantasy XV]]'' was also a major success, selling millions. There were also other Japanese RPGs that earned commercial success and/or critical acclaim that year, including ''[[Dragon Quest VII: Fragments of the Forgotten Past]]'', ''[[Shin Megami Tensei IV: Apocalypse]]'', ''[[Bravely Second]]'', ''[[Fire Emblem Fates]]'', ''[[Dragon Quest Builders]]'', ''[[World of Final Fantasy]]'', ''[[Exist Archive]]'', and ''[[I am Setsuna]]''.<ref name="technobuffalo2016"/>

==South Korean role-playing games<span id="Korea"></span>==
{{Main|Video gaming in South Korea}}
{{See also|:Category:Video games developed in South Korea|l1=Video games developed in South Korea|History of massively multiplayer online games}}

===1980s–1990s===
South Korea's RPG industry began in the early 1980/ with licensed and translated versions of international titles. Later on, The country's first fully-fledged computer RPG was ''Sin'geom-ui Jeonseol'', also known as ''Legend of the Sword'', released for the [[Apple II]] computer platform in 1987. It was programmed by Nam In-Hwan and distributed by Aproman, and was primarily influenced by the ''[[Ultima (series)|Ultima]]'' series. In the late 1980s, the Korean company Topia began producing [[action role-playing game]]s, one of which was ''Pungnyu Hyeopgaek'' for the [[MS-DOS]] in 1989. It was the first Korean title published for [[IBM PC compatible]]s and is set in [[ancient Korea]] and [[ancient China]]. Another action RPG released by Topia that same year was ''Mirae Sonyeon Conan'', a video game adaptation of [[Hayao Miyazaki]]'s Japanese 1978 [[anime]] series ''[[Future Boy Conan]]'', for the [[MSX2]] platform.<ref>{{cite web|title=Part 1: First steps and emancipation (1976–1993)|url=http://www.hardcoregaming101.net/korea/part1/korea1.htm|work=A History of Korean Gaming|publisher=Hardcore Gaming 101|access-date=6 September 2011|author=Derboo|date=13 July 2010}}</ref>

1994 saw the release of two major Korean RPGs: ''[[Astonishia Story]]'', and an [[MS-DOS]] [[Video game remake|enhanced remake]] ''[[Ys II: Ancient Ys Vanished – The Final Chapter|Ys II Special]]'', developed by Mantra.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hyeon |first=Namil |date= 23 October 2008 |script-title=ko:국산 RPG의 전설, 어스토니시아 스토리 |url=https://www.thisisgame.com/articles/9335 |website=ThisIsGAme |access-date=10 August 2025}}</ref> The latter was a mash-up of [[Nihon Falcom]]'s game ''Ys II'' (1988) with the anime ''[[Ys (anime)|Ys II: Castle in the Heavens]]'' (1992) along with a large amount of new content, including more secrets than any other version of ''Ys II''. Both games were a success in Korea, ''Astonishia Story'' more so.<ref name="gtm_falcom_157">{{cite journal|last=Szczepaniak|first=John|title=Falcom: Legacy of Ys|journal=[[GamesTM|Games<sup>TM</sup>]]|date=7 July 2011|issue=111|pages=152–159 [157]|url=http://imageshack.us/f/718/yshistory06.jpg/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120710170517/http://imageshack.us/f/718/yshistory06.jpg/|url-status=dead|archive-date=10 July 2012|access-date=9 September 2011}} ([[cf.]] {{cite web|last=Szczepaniak|first=John|title=History of Ys interviews|url=http://blog.hardcoregaming101.net/2011/07/history-of-ys-interviews-by-john.html|work=Hardcore Gaming 101|access-date=9 September 2011|date=8 July 2011}})</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Szczepaniak|first=John|title=Falcom: Legacy of Ys|journal=[[GamesTM|Games<sup>TM</sup>]]|date=7 July 2011|issue=111|pages=152–159 [158]|url=http://imageshack.us/f/841/yshistory07.jpg/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120709121419/http://imageshack.us/f/841/yshistory07.jpg/|url-status=dead|archive-date=9 July 2012|access-date=10 September 2011}} ([[cf.]] {{cite web|last=Szczepaniak|first=John|title=History of Ys interviews|url=http://blog.hardcoregaming101.net/2011/07/history-of-ys-interviews-by-john.html|work=Hardcore Gaming 101|access-date=10 September 2011|date=8 July 2011}})</ref>

Commercial [[online game|online gaming]] became very popular in South Korea from the mid-1990s. ''[[Nexus: The Kingdom of the Winds]]'', designed by Jake Song, was commercially released in 1996 and eventually gained over one million subscribers. It was one of the earliest [[massively multiplayer online role-playing game]]s. Song's next game, ''[[Lineage (video game)|Lineage]]'' (1998), enjoyed even greater success gaining millions of subscribers in Korea and Taiwan. This helped to secure developer [[NCsoft]]'s dominance in the global MMORPG market for several years.<!--This would be a good place to throw 1 or 2 sentences listing NCSoft's other MMORPG achievements and the years they went live-->

===2000s–present===
In 2002, the [[Sprite (computer graphics)|sprite]]-based ''[[Ragnarok Online]]'', produced by Korean company [[Gravity (Korean company)|Gravity Corp]], was released. Though unknown to many Western players, the game took Asia by storm as ''Lineage'' had done. The publisher has claimed in excess of 25 million subscribers of the game, although this number is based upon a quantity of registered users (rather than active subscribers).<ref>Michael Kanellos (2004), "Gaming their Way to Growth", [http://news.cnet.com/Consumers+Gaming+their+way+to+growth+-+Part+3+of+South+Koreas+Digital+Dynasty/2009-1040_3-5239555.html CNET News]</ref> 2002 also saw the release of ''[[MapleStory]]'', another sprite-based title, which was completely [[free-to-play]]—instead of charging a monthly fee, it generated revenue by selling in-game "enhancements". ''MapleStory'' would go on to become a major player in the new market for free-to-play MMORPGs (generating huge numbers of registered accounts across its many versions), if it did not introduce the market by itself.

In October 2003, ''[[Lineage II]]'' (NCsoft's sequel to ''Lineage'') became the latest MMORPG to achieve huge success across Asia. It received the Presidential Award at the 2003 Korean Game awards. As of the first half of 2005, ''Lineage II'' counted over 2.25 million subscribers worldwide, with servers in Japan, China, North America, Taiwan, and Europe, once the popularity of the game had surged in the West. To date, the ''Lineage'' franchise has attracted 43 million players.<ref>{{cite magazine | url=https://www.forbes.com/2006/08/02/bestselling-video-games-cx_de_0802mario.html | title=The Best-Selling Videogame Franchises | access-date=21 March 2009 | date=2 August 2006 | last=Ewalt | first=David M. | magazine=[[Forbes]]}}</ref>

==Chinese and Taiwanese role-playing games<span id="China"></span>==
{{See also|Video games in China|Video games in Taiwan|l2=Video games developed in Taiwan|:Category:Video games developed in Hong Kong|l3=Video games developed in Hong Kong}}

''Ruyiji'' was released in Taiwan in 1986. It's a [[role-playing game]] and the first commercial Chinese game.<ref>Game Professional Introduction (2nd Edition) (Ninth Art Academy – Game Development Series)(Chinese Edition), Tsinghua University Press (2015), P. 295</ref>

''[[Xuan-Yuan Sword]]'', a Taiwanese role-playing game based on [[Chinese mythology]], was released in 1990. It has become a series and its latest sequel was released in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/chinese-action-rpg-xuan-yuan-sword-7-hits-october-29th-with-a-demo-available-now/|title=Chinese action RPG Xuan-Yuan Sword 7 hits October 29th with a demo available now|website=[[PC Gamer]] |date=12 October 2020}}</ref>

''[[Heroes of Jin Yong]]'' (1996), a Taiwanese [[tactical role-playing game]] based on the popular historical [[wuxia]] novels by [[Jin Yong]], featured a number of melee and ranged [[kung fu]] skills to train and develop, as well as a grid-based movement system.

China has a number of domestically produced games. These include ''[[Westward Journey Online II|Westward Journey]]'', ''[[Perfect World (video game)|Perfect World]]'', and ''[[The Incorruptible Warrior]]''. There are a large number of domestically-produced [[Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|MMORPGs]] in China, although many generally remain unheard of outside the country.<ref name="chinageeks">{{cite web | last=Custer | first=Charlie | title=Chinese Video Games in America | date=24 January 2010 | publisher=ChinaGeeks | url=http://chinageeks.org/2010/01/chinese-video-games-in-america/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160120063030/http://chinageeks.org/2010/01/chinese-video-games-in-america/ | url-status=dead | archive-date=20 January 2016 | access-date=20 January 2016}}</ref>

''[[Genshin Impact]]'' (2020), a Chinese [[Open world|open-world]] [[action role-playing game]], features an action-based battle system involving elemental magic and character switching, and it also uses [[gacha game]] [[Video game monetization|monetization]] for players to obtain new characters, weapons, and other resources.<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Fenlon|first=Wes|date=28 September 2020|title=Genshin Impact, an ambitious Chinese RPG inspired by Breath of the Wild, is out today|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/genshin-impact-an-ambitious-chinese-rpg-inspired-by-breath-of-the-wild-is-out-today/|access-date=29 September 2020|magazine=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Romano|first=Sal |date=22 July 2020|title=Genshin Impact due out by October for PC, iOS, and Android; second closed beta test for PS4 begins July 30|url=https://www.gematsu.com/2020/07/genshin-impact-due-out-by-october-for-pc-ios-and-android-second-closed-beta-test-for-ps4-begins-july-30|access-date=29 September 2020|website=Gematsu}}</ref> According to some media reports, ''Genshin Impact'' was the biggest international launch of any Chinese video game at the time of its release.<ref name="scmp">{{cite news |last=Ye|first=Josh |title=Genshin Impact works its magic to become biggest global launch of a Chinese game ever, analysts say |url=https://www.scmp.com/tech/apps-social/article/3103522/genshin-impact-works-its-magic-become-biggest-global-launch |work=[[South China Morning Post]] |date=30 September 2020|access-date=20 October 2020}}</ref><ref name="SensorTowerFirstWeek">{{cite web |last=Chapple |first=Craig |title=Genshin Impact Generates $60 Million in First Week as it Becomes World's No. 2 Grossing Mobile Game |url=https://sensortower.com/blog/genshin-impact-first-week-revenue |website=Sensor Tower |date=6 October 2020|access-date=10 October 2020}}</ref>

==Criticism==
Japanese developer [[Naoki Yoshida]], known for [[Dragon Quest]] and [[Final Fantasy]], stated in an interview with SkillUp through a translator that the development team doesn't think of their games as "JRPG". He said the term first appeared "15 years ago" and was thought of as discriminatory. Specifically recalling media referring to [[Final Fantasy 7]] as a "JRPG" in a way of "compartmentalizing". Yoshida thought these feeling of "being made fun of" may remain as a memory.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gerblick |first1=Jordan |title=Final Fantasy visionary Yoshi-P really doesn't like the term JRPG |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/final-fantasy-visionary-yoshi-p-really-doesnt-like-the-term-jrpg/ |website=GamesRadar+ |date=28 February 2023}}</ref> ''Inverse'' opined afterwards that JRPG is "archaic" and it is better to use alternatives.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Madsen |first1=Hayes |title=Yoshi-P Is Right: It's Time to Retire "JRPG" |url=https://www.inverse.com/gaming/jrpg-meaning-offensive-naoki-yoshida |website=Inverse |date=20 February 2024}}</ref>

======================================================================
WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: Mad Max (2015 video game)
======================================================================

{{short description|2015 video game}}
{{good article}}{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2015}}
{{Infobox video game

'''''Mad Max''''' is a 2015 [[Action-adventure game|action-adventure]] [[video game]] based on the ''[[Mad Max]]'' franchise developed by [[Avalanche Studios]] and published by [[Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment]]. The game follows [[Max Rockatansky]] as he progresses through the wasteland building a vehicle, the ''Magnum Opus'', to battle against a gang of hostile raiders led by Scabrous Scrotus and reach the storied "Plains of Silence", where he hopes to find peace. ''Mad Max'' emphasizes [[Vehicular combat game|vehicular combat]], in which players can use weapon and armor upgrades on their car to fight enemies. It is set in an [[open world]], a [[Apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic fiction|post-apocalyptic]] wasteland consisting of deserts, canyons, and caves. The game adopted a free-flowing combat system, similar to [[Rocksteady Studios]]' ''[[Batman: Arkham]]'' series.

Two other ''Mad Max'' games, developed by [[Cory Barlog]] and [[Interplay Entertainment]] respectively, were in production before the announcement of this game, but neither of them were successfully released. Although ''Mad Max'' is not based on a specific film in the series, it was inspired by its universe, features locations that appear in the films, and franchise co-creator [[George Miller (director)|George Miller]] was consulted during the game's pre-production. Avalanche Studios found developing a vehicular-combat video game a challenge because of their inexperience with creating that type of game. Unlike Avalanche's previous games like the ''[[Just Cause (video game series)|Just Cause]]'' series, ''Mad Max'' had a more mature tone. The game was re-tooled a year into development, as the studio pivoted from making ''Mad Max'' a linear experience to an open world game.

Announced at [[E3 2013]] and originally planned for release in 2014, ''Mad Max'' was released in September the following year, several months after the theatrical release of ''[[Mad Max: Fury Road]]'', the fourth film in the series, for [[PlayStation 4]], [[Windows]], and [[Xbox One]]. [[Feral Interactive]] published the game's [[Linux]] and [[macOS]] versions, while the [[PlayStation 3]] and [[Xbox 360]] versions were canceled. ''Mad Max'' received mixed reviews from critics. Although the game's environment, direction, vehicular combat, and graphics were praised, its quest design and story were criticized. The game underperformed commercially, with former CEO of Avalanche Studios Christofer Sundberg attributing its underwhelming performance to going on sale on the same day as ''[[Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain]]''. Plans to release [[downloadable content]] packs for the game were scrapped.

==Gameplay==
[[File:Mad Max gameplay screenshot.png|thumb|alt=Game screenshot of a car chase through a canyon|Gameplay screenshot showcasing vehicular combat|left]]
''Mad Max'' is an [[Action-adventure game|action-adventure]] game set in an [[open world]] [[Apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic fiction|post-apocalyptic]] environment caused by resource shortages and [[ecocide]].<ref>{{Cite book |title=Avenging nature: the role of nature in modern and contemporary art and literature |date=2020 |publisher=Lexington Books |isbn=978-1-7936-2144-3 |editor-last=Valls Oyarzun |editor-first=Eduardo |series=Ecocritical theory and practice |location=Lanham Boulder NewYork London |chapter=17 |editor-last2=Gualberto Valverde |editor-first2=Rebeca |editor-last3=Malla García |editor-first3=Noelia |editor-last4=Colom Jiménez |editor-first4=María |editor-last5=Cordero Sánchez |editor-first5=Rebeca}}</ref> It emphasizes [[Vehicular combat game|vehicular combat]], in which the player is the eponymous Mad Max. According to its publisher, up to 60 percent of the game focuses on driving.<ref name="Poly on Gameplay"/> Some weapons and tools, including flamethrowers and turbo boosts, are mounted directly onto the ''Magnum Opus'', while others, such as a harpoon and sniper rifle, are used in conjunction with the vehicle by Chumbucket, Max's assistant, or Max himself. Max's ''Magnum Opus'', with its V8 engine and powerful ramming ability, can destroy enemies' vehicles and weaponry.<ref name="GI Feature 1">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/13/behind-the-wheel-of-mad-maxs-open-world-vehicular-combat.aspx|title=Behind The Wheel Of Mad Max's Vehicular Combat|first=Tim|last=Turi|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|date=13 March 2015|access-date=26 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150424062649/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/13/behind-the-wheel-of-mad-maxs-open-world-vehicular-combat.aspx|archive-date=24 April 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> When simultaneously driving and aiming, the game changes to slow motion<ref>{{cite web|url=http://metro.co.uk/2015/06/25/mad-max-hands-on-preview-fallout-on-wheels-5264517/|title=Mad Max hands-on preview – Fallout on wheels|work=[[Metro (magazine)|Metro]]|date=25 June 2015|access-date=1 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150701215348/http://metro.co.uk/2015/06/25/mad-max-hands-on-preview-fallout-on-wheels-5264517/|archive-date=1 July 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> to allow the player to toggle between targets. Although ''Mad Max'' primarily uses a [[Third-person (video games)|third-person perspective]], the player can switch to [[First-person (video games)|first-person view]] when fighting enemies while driving the ''Magnum Opus''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamesradar.com/mad-max-has-creative-approaches-combat-and-first-person-mode/?hootPostID=1b22b683a47f1d55553183418c87e85e|title=Mad Max has 'creative approaches to combat' and a first person mode|first=Louise|last=Blain|work=[[GamesRadar]]|date=25 March 2015|access-date=26 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526215714/http://www.gamesradar.com/mad-max-has-creative-approaches-combat-and-first-person-mode/?hootPostID=1b22b683a47f1d55553183418c87e85e|archive-date=26 May 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Chumbucket repairs the car when instructed to do so or when the player exits.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2015-05-25-mad-max-preview|title=The Mad Max game takes a different path to Fury Road|first=Aoife|last=Wilson|work=[[Eurogamer]]|date=26 May 2015|access-date=26 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526180520/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2015-05-25-mad-max-preview|archive-date=26 May 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

To encourage exploration, the ''Magnum Opus'' can be upgraded with materials scavenged from the desert, by hijacking enemies' cars or collecting their car parts.<ref name="Poly on Gameplay">{{cite web|url=http://www.polygon.com/features/2015/5/26/8656261/mad-max-car-combat-avalanche|title=Mad Max is Melee Car Combat in an Open Wasteland|first=Colin|last=Campbell|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=26 May 2015|access-date=26 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526180020/http://www.polygon.com/features/2015/5/26/8656261/mad-max-car-combat-avalanche|archive-date=26 May 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="GIfeat">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/06/10-badass-things-we-did-in-mad-maxs-open-world.aspx?PostPageIndex=2|title=10 Badass Things We Did In Mad Max's Open World|first=Tim|last=Turi|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|date=6 March 2015|access-date=26 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150325061206/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/06/10-badass-things-we-did-in-mad-maxs-open-world.aspx?PostPageIndex=2|archive-date=25 March 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> An enemy can jump on top of the ''Magnum Opus'' to make it explode, but the player can avoid that by surrounding the car with hazards such as spikes.<ref name="GI Feature 1"/> The player can access the garage screen throughout the game, allowing them to customize the ''Magnum Opus''. Max's garage can change and modify the car's engine, chassis, wheels, body work, paint job, and its "shell".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.playstationlifestyle.net/2015/06/21/mad-max-game-preview-grappling-with-fun-e3-2015/#/slide/1|title=E3 2015 – Mad Max Hands-On Preview: Grappling With Fun|first=Dan|last=Oravasaari|work=[[PlayStation LifeStyle]]|date=21 June 2015|access-date=22 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623162300/http://www.playstationlifestyle.net/2015/06/21/mad-max-game-preview-grappling-with-fun-e3-2015/#/slide/1|archive-date=23 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Upgrading one aspect of the car will negatively affect other aspects; upgrading the engine will allow Max to drive faster, but handling will be more difficult.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/16/building-your-nightmarish-dream-car-in-mad-max.aspx?PostPageIndex=2|title=Building Your Nightmarish Dream Car In Mad Max|first=Tim|last=Turi|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|date=16 March 2015|access-date=26 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150320203947/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/16/building-your-nightmarish-dream-car-in-mad-max.aspx?PostPageIndex=2|archive-date=20 March 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> The sound produced by the engine changes when the player changes, adds, or remove parts of the ''Magnum Opus''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamesradar.com/mad-maxs-audio-lets-you-recognise-you-car-sound-and-even-models-echos/|title=Mad Max's audio lets you recognise your car by sound and even models echos|first=Dom|last=Reseigh-Lincoln|work=[[GamesRadar]]|date=11 July 2015|access-date=11 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150712171209/http://www.gamesradar.com/mad-maxs-audio-lets-you-recognise-you-car-sound-and-even-models-echos/|archive-date=12 July 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Max, his armor, and weapons are customisable;<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/mad-max-gameplay-reveal-trailer-shows-punishing-wa/1100-6426836/|title=Mad Max Gameplay Reveal Trailer Shows Punishing Wasteland|first=Eddie|last=Makuch|work=[[GameSpot]]|date=23 April 2015|access-date=26 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150425210612/http://www.gamespot.com/articles/mad-max-gameplay-reveal-trailer-shows-punishing-wa/1100-6426836/|archive-date=25 April 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> the player can unlock new skills and upgrades for him as he progresses through the game and earns [[experience (gaming)|experience points]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ibtimes.co.in/five-reasons-why-you-should-play-mad-max-game-643137|title=Five Reasons Why You Should Play the Mad Max Game|first=Prarthito|last=Maity|work=[[iDigitalTimes]]|date=17 August 2015|access-date=1 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150824060209/http://www.ibtimes.co.in/five-reasons-why-you-should-play-mad-max-game-643137|archive-date=24 August 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Max is also customisable, with his clothing, appearance, fighting skills, and weapons being modifiable. Griffa, a wasteland wanderer, also offers Max tokens which can be used to upgrade his abilities.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pcgamer.com/mad-max-guide-tips/|title=Mad Max tips: 12 things we wish we'd known before we started|first=Christopher|last=Livington|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=9 September 2015|access-date=21 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160613071100/http://www.pcgamer.com/mad-max-guide-tips/|archive-date=13 June 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>

''Mad Max'' features a variety of weapons, including Max's iconic shotgun, but ammunition is scarce and the game emphasizes melee combat over firearms.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usgamer.net/articles/mad-max-walkthrough-and-guide-clear-all-camps-scrap-locations-find-all-history-relics|title=Mad Max Walkthrough and Guide|work=[[USgamer]]|date=9 April 2015|access-date=21 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160607184547/http://www.usgamer.net/articles/mad-max-walkthrough-and-guide-clear-all-camps-scrap-locations-find-all-history-relics|archive-date=7 June 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> One weapon is the explosive Thunderstick, which can be lanced into an enemy's chest.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2015/04/23/new-mad-max-trailer-offers-a-load-of-gameplay-details|title=New Mad Max Trailer Offers A Load of Gameplay Details|work=[[IGN]]|first=Wesley|last=Copeland|date=23 April 2015|access-date=26 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150426015315/http://www.ign.com/articles/2015/04/23/new-mad-max-trailer-offers-a-load-of-gameplay-details|archive-date=26 April 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> The game has a free-flow combat system combining [[professional wrestling attacks]] and [[boxing]] techniques, similar to Warner Bros.' previous ''[[Batman: Arkham]]'' video-game series (in which indicators on enemies' heads remind the player when to strike, counter or make finishing moves). Attacks by Max during his "frenzied" state are more powerful than usual.<ref name="GSpot on Gameplay"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.polygon.com/2015/4/23/8479877/max-max-gameplay-trailer-batman-combat-car|title=Mad Max pimps his ride and fights like Batman|first=Dave|last=Tach|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=23 April 2015|access-date=26 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150525220602/http://www.polygon.com/2015/4/23/8479877/max-max-gameplay-trailer-batman-combat-car|archive-date=25 May 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

''Mad Max''{{'}}s landscape consists of canyons, caves, deserts, and abandoned wastelands. The game's world is divided into several regions, with each having its own backstory and landscape. Unique landmarks and ruins can be discovered in each region. Side activities such as races, time trials,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamesradar.com/17-things-i-did-2-hours-wasteland-mad-max/|title=17 chaotic and brutal things I did in 2 hours in the Wasteland in Mad Max|first=Louise|last=Blain|work=[[GamesRadar]]|date=10 July 2015|access-date=11 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150712195846/http://www.gamesradar.com/17-things-i-did-2-hours-wasteland-mad-max/|archive-date=12 July 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> invading enemy fortresses, and eliminating enemy convoys can be found in each region. A region's threat level is lowered by completing these activities, facilitating its navigation.<ref name="GSpot on Gameplay">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/in-mad-max-car-combat-reigns-supreme/1100-6427574/|title=In Mad Max, Car Combat Reigns Supreme|first=Randolph|last=Ramsay|work=[[GameSpot]]|date=26 May 2015|access-date=26 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150528140722/http://www.gamespot.com/articles/in-mad-max-car-combat-reigns-supreme/1100-6427574/|archive-date=28 May 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Each region has a boss, who can be found and defeated in their base.<ref name="PCGPre">{{cite web|url=http://www.pcgamer.com/mad-max-hands-on-too-fast-too-furiosa/|title=Mad Max hands-on: The fast and the Furiosa|first=Evan|last=Lahti|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=26 May 2015|access-date=1 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150528190755/http://www.pcgamer.com/mad-max-hands-on-too-fast-too-furiosa/|archive-date=28 May 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Some of the game's strongholds are friendly, and eliminating hostile strongholds gives Max additional quests and rewards.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vg247.com/2013/09/02/mad-max-an-open-world-destruction-derby-of-pain/|title=Mad Max: an open world destruction derby of pain – interview|first=Dave|last=Cook|work=[[VG247]]|date=2 September 2013|access-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623145022/http://www.vg247.com/2013/09/02/mad-max-an-open-world-destruction-derby-of-pain/|archive-date=23 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> These strongholds can be upgraded, offering Max different benefits such as helping Max to collect scraps when the game is turned off, or restoring Max's health and shotgun ammo upon visits.<ref name="PolyTips"/> Max can ascend in a hot-air balloon (permanently attached to the ground) to look for new objectives and locations. After seeing the objectives through binoculars, they are highlighted on the map.<ref name="GIfeat"/> Max can be guided by Chumbucket in strategically completing his objectives.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.playstationlifestyle.net/2013/06/23/mad-max-ps4-e3-preview/|title=Mad Max (PS4) – E3 Preview|first=Chandler|last=Wood|work=[[PlayStation LifeStyle]]|date=23 June 2013|access-date=26 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526192515/http://www.playstationlifestyle.net/2013/06/23/mad-max-ps4-e3-preview/|archive-date=26 May 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/25/meet-the-weirdos-of-mad-max-s-wasteland.aspx|title=Meet The Weirdos Of Mad Max's Wasteland|first=Jeff|last=Cork|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|date=25 March 2015|access-date=26 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150425180414/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/25/meet-the-weirdos-of-mad-max-s-wasteland.aspx|archive-date=25 April 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Max is accompanied by a dog companion who can detect land mines.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/2015/12/20/the-best-dog-of-2015-fallout-4s-dogmeat-vs-mad-maxs-dinki-di-vs-metal-gears-dd/|title=The best dog of 2015: Fallout 4's Dogmeat vs. Mad Max's Dinki-Di vs. Metal Gear's DD|first=Giancarlo|last=Valdes|work=[[VentureBeat]]|date=20 December 2015|access-date=21 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160530124806/http://venturebeat.com/2015/12/20/the-best-dog-of-2015-fallout-4s-dogmeat-vs-mad-maxs-dinki-di-vs-metal-gears-dd/|archive-date=30 May 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> Max has limited climbing abilities, and objects that he can climb are highlighted in yellow.<ref name="PolyTips">{{cite web|url=http://www.polygon.com/2015/9/3/9254097/mad-max-tips-guide-ps4-playstation-4-xbox-one-windows-pc|title=Six Tips For Getting Most Out Of Mad Max's Wasteland|first=Phillip|last=Kollar|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=3 September 2015|access-date=21 June 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>

Most resources in the game are scarce except for gasoline, which is needed for driving. The player can collect one [[jerrycan]] at a time, storing it in the back of the ''Magnum Opus'',<ref name="GRadar">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamesradar.com/mad-max-feature-driven-distraction/|title=Driven to distraction – how Mad Max is dropping a bomb on the open-world|first=Joe|last=Skrebels|work=[[GamesRadar]]|date=21 April 2015|access-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623150522/http://www.gamesradar.com/mad-max-feature-driven-distraction/|archive-date=23 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> and can find collectibles (history relics) throughout the game. The relics are primarily photos and notes of the wasteland before the apocalypse.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/27/mad-max-wasteland-lore-101.aspx?PostPageIndex=2|title=Mad Max Wasteland Lore 101|first=Jeff|last=Cork|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|date=27 March 2015|access-date=26 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150817092242/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/27/mad-max-wasteland-lore-101.aspx?PostPageIndex=2|archive-date=17 August 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Food and water are vital to Max's survival; the player can collect them in the wasteland and use them to replenish their [[health (gaming)|health]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pushsquare.com/news/2015/03/youll_have_to_find_food_and_water_to_survive_in_ps4s_mad_max_plus_more_dusty_gameplay_details|title=You'll Have to Find Food and Water to Survive in PS4's Mad Max, Plus More Dusty Gameplay Details|first=Robert|last=Ramsey|work=Push Square|date=6 March 2015|access-date=1 July September 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Max can also eat small animals, such as rodents, and maggots from decomposing corpses, to replenish his health, and areas where he can find food and supplies have crows flying around them.<ref name="IGN Gameplay 1">{{cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2015/03/03/new-mad-max-gameplay-details-emerge|title=New Mad Max Gameplay Details Emerge|first=Jordan|last=Sirani|work=[[IGN]]|date=3 March 2015|access-date=26 March described, the player would be able to venture into the Big Nothing, an uncharted, volatile area of the wasteland with dangerous sandstorms and no food or water in which rare parts for the ''Magnum Opus'' could be found (according to Avalanche, the "Big Nothing" made the game map infinite<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2015/08/28/mad-max-is-1080p-on-xbox-one-and-ps4-map-isnt-finite|title=Mad Max Is 1080p On Xbox One and PS4, Map Isn't 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>) but ultimately this was not a feature of the final gameplay. A dynamic day-night cycle, a weather system and a variety of environmental hazards are included in the game,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.us.playstation.com/2015/04/23/first-look-at-mad-max-gameplay/|title=First Look at Mad Max Gameplay|first=John|last=Fuller|work=PlayStation Blog|publisher=[[Avalanche Studios]]|date=23 April 2015|access-date=26 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518084812/http://blog.us.playstation.com/2015/04/23/first-look-at-mad-max-gameplay/|archive-date=18 May 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> whose terrain is affected by weather and natural disasters.<ref name="Poly on Gameplay"/>

== Plot ==
Highway patrol officer-turned-survivalist [[Max Rockatansky]] ([[Bren Foster]]) journeys in search of what he calls the Plains of Silence. He runs into War Boys led by Scabrous Scrotus ([[Travis Willingham]]), son of [[Immortan Joe]] and ruler of Gastown. The War Boys run Max off the road and steal his car and supplies, leaving him to die in the desert. Max chases them and duels Scrotus on top of his vehicle, the Land Mover. Scrotus sics his war hound on Max, but after Max fends off the dog, Scrotus throws it aside in disgust. Max then stabs Scrotus in the head with his own chainsaw, but Scrotus, with the broken chainsaw blade still stuck in his head, kicks Max off the Land Mover.<ref name="Poly sources">{{cite web|url=http://www.polygon.com/2013/6/12/4420854/mad-max-avalanche-studios-game-e3 |title=Mad Max borrows the series' bombastic elements to create a new, open-world adventure |last=Corriea |first=Alexa Ray |publisher=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |date=12 June 2013 |access-date=21 August 2013}}</ref>

Max obtains a weapon and clothes from a dead Wastelander, cares for the wounded dog, and resolves to find Scrotus's base of operations and recover his car. In the desert, Max meets a hunchbacked mechanic named Chumbucket ([[Jason Spisak]]). Max agrees to find parts for Chumbucket's project, a car he calls the Magnum Opus; Chumbucket believes that Max has been sent by God to aid him and addresses him as "Warrior Saint". Max must first liberate Wasteland leaders' territories from the War Boys: Jeet ([[Josh Keaton]]), whose stronghold is in an old lighthouse, and Gut Gash ([[Liam O'Brien]]), whose followers believe that they will be protected from a flood in their ship stronghold built on the remains of an oil tanker. Chumbucket builds an exploding harpoon launcher for the Magnum Opus, allowing Max to destroy a massive gate protected by War Boys and explore new territory. Max and Chumbucket must then save Pink Eye ([[Adrienne Barbeau]]), a woman whose mechanical skill rivals Chumbucket's, from an invasion of her silo base led by Stank Gum—one of Scrotus' Top Dogs.

Searching for a V8 engine for the Magnum Opus, Max learns about a race in Gastown with a Big Chief V8 as a prize. After winning the race against Stank Gum ([[Yuri Lowenthal]]) and defeating the fighter Tenderloin in a Thunderdome duel, Max receives the engine and the concubine Hope ([[Courtenay Taylor]]). His victory is short-lived; Scrotus recognizes Max and attacks him. After he is shot with a crossbow and thrown down a mine shaft, Max is saved by Hope, who takes him to the medic Organic Mechanic ([[Fred Tatasciore]]) and his blood donor Scab (Orion Acaba) before Max loses consciousness. While he is undergoing surgery, he has a hallucination of marrying Hope, officiated by Chumbucket and a man with a dog's head. When he wakes up, he and Hope steal the Big Chief; they drive to the temple of Deep Friah ([[Robin Atkin Downes]]), a friendly fire cultist.

At the temple, Hope asks Max to find her daughter Glory (Madison Carlon), who had fled to Buzzard territory. He travels to the Underdune and rescues Glory from the Buzzards. Returning, he discovers that Chumbucket has taken the Magnum Opus to his old home. Max follows him in one of Deep Friah's cars, but learns that Scrotus and Stank Gum tortured Chumbucket, who revealed Hope and Glory's location and their ties to Max. Max kills Stank Gum, rushes back to the temple and finds Hope hanged and Glory tortured on the floor. Glory dies in his arms, and Max swears vengeance against Scrotus.

He returns to Gastown and learns Scrotus' location from Scab. Max and Chumbucket find Scrotus driving around the Purgatory Flatlands, and after a prolonged chase the Land Mover is left teetering on the edge of a cliff. Over Chumbucket's protests, Max rams the wreck with the Magnum Opus, leaping clear while Chumbucket is killed and both vehicles are sent over the cliff. Scrotus reappears driving Max's Interceptor, and the two fight on until Max pulls the chainsaw blade back out of Scrotus' head, killing him. Max enters the Interceptor, restores a picture of his family to the dashboard, and drives away.

==Development==
[[File:George Miller SDCC 2014.jpg|thumb|right|150px|[[George Miller (director)|George Miller]] provided input during the game's pre-production period.]]
A video game set in the ''Mad Max'' universe was mentioned by franchise creator [[George Miller (director)|George Miller]] in a 2008 interview.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blog.newsweek.com/blogs/levelup/archive/2008/03/12/the-george-miller-interview-part-ii.aspx |title=The George Miller Interview, Part II |first=N'Gai |last=Croal |work=Newseeker |date=12 March 2008 |access-date=26 May 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080921175439/http://blog.newsweek.com/blogs/levelup/archive/2008/03/12/the-george-miller-interview-part-ii.aspx |archive-date=21 September 2008 }}</ref> Miller joined ''[[God of War II]]'' director [[Cory Barlog]] to develop the game after Barlog left [[Sony Computer Entertainment]]. The project was originally intended as a tie-in with a ''Mad Max'' animated film which would be released simultaneously. The film's production was suspended to allow adequate production time for the game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2008/03/film-legend-god-of-war-2-director-announce-mad-max-game/|title=Film legend, God of War 2 director announce Mad Max game|first=Michael|last=Thompson|work=[[Ars Technica]]|date=14 March 2008|access-date=26 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526193440/http://arstechnica.com/gaming/2008/03/film-legend-god-of-war-2-director-announce-mad-max-game/|archive-date=26 May 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> After Barlog announced in 2008 that a publisher for the game was being sought, no further information about the project was forthcoming.<ref name="GRadar 2 Mad Max"/> In 2010, Barlog was a consultant for [[Avalanche Studios]], leaving in 2012 for [[Crystal Dynamics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vg247.com/2012/03/02/cory-barlog-heads-to-crystal-dynamics/|title=Cory Barlog heads to Crystal Dynamics|first=Johnny|last=Cullen|work=[[VG247]]|date=2 March 2012|access-date=26 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526202459/http://www.vg247.com/2012/03/02/cory-barlog-heads-to-crystal-dynamics/|archive-date=26 May 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> A ''[[Mad Max: Fury Road]]'' tie-in video game was in development by [[Interplay Entertainment]], but was scrapped when [[Electronic Arts]] acquired the franchise's video-game rights for $20 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/fallout-dev-was-working-on-mad-max-game-here-s-wha/1100-6427420/|title=Fallout Dev Was Working on Mad Max Game, Here's What Happened to It|first=Tamoor|last=Hussain|date=18 May 2015|access-date=26 May 2015|work=[[GameSpot]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150522043718/http://www.gamespot.com/articles/fallout-dev-was-working-on-mad-max-game-here-s-wha/1100-6427420/|archive-date=22 May 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Avalanche Studios]] revealed that they were working on the game in 2013. Avalanche's founder and CEO Christofer Sundburg said that Miller and Barlog's project was not the ''Mad Max'' game announced by Avalanche, though Barlog briefly worked on a ''Mad Max'' game while working at Avalanche.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.polygon.com/2013/6/17/4439142/mad-max-maker-says-he-wasnt-making-the-mad-max-he-was-rumored-to-be|title=Mad Max maker says he wasn't making the Mad Max he was rumored to be making (update)|first=Chris|last=Plante|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=17 July 2013|access-date=26 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150524051359/http://www.polygon.com/2013/6/17/4439142/mad-max-maker-says-he-wasnt-making-the-mad-max-he-was-rumored-to-be|archive-date=24 May 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Miller had collaborated with Avalanche during the game's pre-production in mid-2011.<ref name="GRadar 2 Mad Max">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamesradar.com/george-millar-was-involved-mad-max-game/?hootPostID=c98d58c0c07c070a0722053495550ed2|title=The Mad Max game's had a confusing life but George Miller was involved "super early on"|work=[[GamesRadar]]|date=26 May 2015|access-date=26 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526215721/http://www.gamesradar.com/george-millar-was-involved-mad-max-game/?hootPostID=c98d58c0c07c070a0722053495550ed2|archive-date=26 May 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> The game was not intended to be a [[tie-in]] for ''Fury Road'';<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.shacknews.com/article/80824/mad-max-not-a-movie-tie-in-says-avalanche-game|title=Mad Max not a movie tie-in, says Avalanche game designer|first=Ozzie|last=Mejia|work=[[Shacknews]]|date=22 August 2013|access-date=26 May setting and story are original.<ref name="IGN stealth">{{cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2013/06/12/e3-2013-harpoon-dudes-in-the-face-in-mad-max|title=E3 2013: Harpoon Dudes In the Face of Mad Max|first=Justin|last=Davis|work=[[IGN]]|date=11 June 2015|access-date=26 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526200000/http://www.ign.com/articles/2013/06/12/e3-2013-harpoon-dudes-in-the-face-in-mad-max|archive-date=26 May 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> This decision was made because the game's publisher, [[Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment]], believed that a standalone game was more beneficial to players than a "play-the-movie game" after the success of its ''Batman: Arkham'' series.<ref name="VentureBeat1">{{cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/2015/05/26/avalanche-studios-road-to-the-mad-max-savage-road-game-was-long-and-twisted/|title=The road to Mad Max game was long and twisted for Avalanche Studios|first=Dean|last=Takahashi|work=[[VentureBeat]]|date=26 May 2015|access-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150616235233/http://venturebeat.com/2015/05/26/avalanche-studios-road-to-the-mad-max-savage-road-game-was-long-and-twisted/|archive-date=16 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Locations which have appeared in the films, such as Gas Town and Thunderdome, are featured in the game.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/05/21/10-things-mad-max-fury-road-has-in-common-with-the-upcoming-game.aspx?PostPageIndex=1|title=10 Things Mad Max: Fury Road Shares With The Upcoming Game|first=Tim|last=Turi|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|date=21 May 2015|access-date=1 June June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2015/04/23/mad-max-trailers-reveals-thunderdome-the-iconic-caged-arena-from-third-film|title=Mad Max Trailer Reveals Thunderdome, The Iconic Caged Arena From The Third Film|first=Chloi|last=Rad|work=[[IGN]]|date=23 April 2015|access-date=1 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Full production of the game began before May 2012.<ref name="MillerAvalanche">{{cite web|url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2015-05-25-mad-max-preview|title=The Mad Max game takes a different path to Fury Road|first=Aoife|last=Wilson|website=[[Eurogamer]]|date=5 June 2015|access-date=21 June game was retooled during development.<ref name="VentureBeat1"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.polygon.com/2013/6/10/4416956/mad-max-avalanche-studios-ps4 |title=Mad Max game coming in 2014 to PC, PS4, Xbox One, PS3, Xbox 360 from Avalanche Studios (update) |last=Sarkar |first=Samit |publisher=Polygon |date=10 June 2013 |access-date=21 August 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130808014545/http://www.polygon.com/2013/6/10/4416956/mad-max-avalanche-studios-ps4 |archive-date=8 August 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> It was revealed in 2024 that the studio, despite its experience in working on open world games, were forced to make ''Mad Max'' a linear experience during the game's first year of development.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/mad-max-developer-hits-back-at-film-director-george-miller-after-claim-game-wasnt-as-good-as-he-wanted-it-to-be|title=Mad Max developer hits back at film director George Miller after claim game "wasn't as good as [he] wanted it to be"|first=Ed|last=Nightingale|work=[[Eurogamer]]|date=May 24, 2024|accessdate=May 25, 2024}}</ref>

Unlike previous Avalanche games, such as ''[[Just Cause 2]]'', the game's tone is more mature<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.polygon.com/2014/2/12/5404214/just-cause-3-avalanche-studios|title=Just Cause, Mad Max and the future of Avalanche Studios|first=Brian|last=Crecente|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=12 February 2014|access-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150627033641/http://www.polygon.com/2014/2/12/5404214/just-cause-3-avalanche-studios|archive-date=27 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> and its narrative is emphasized.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.engadget.com/2013/08/22/mad-max-story-is-standalone-because-movie-tie-in-games-tend-to/|title=Mad Max story is standalone because 'movie tie-in games tend to be bad'|first=Sinan|last=Kubba|date=22 August 2013|work=[[Joystiq]]|access-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150703175857/http://www.engadget.com/2013/08/22/mad-max-story-is-standalone-because-movie-tie-in-games-tend-to/|archive-date=3 July 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Similar to the films, Max seldom speaks or expresses emotion; his thoughts are reflected by his actions. According to the team, Max is traumatized by past experiences (such as losing his family); this makes him "insane", "unstable", and "mad". These qualities are reflected in the game's "rage" mode, in which Max inflicts additional damage on enemies.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/23/meet-mad-max-saint-of-the-wasteland-avalanche-studios.aspx|title=Meet Mad Max, Saint Of The Wasteland|first=Tim|last=Turi|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|date=23 March 2015|access-date=1 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150629222223/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/23/meet-mad-max-saint-of-the-wasteland-avalanche-studios.aspx|archive-date=29 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Gaming journalists invited to preview at E3 2013 noted that Max had an American accent, rather than the Australian accent of the film series, and fans protested his new American voice.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kotaku.com.au/2013/06/the-new-mad-max-game-looks-great-but/ |title=The New Mad Max Game Looks Great But... |last=Serrels |first=Mark |work=[[Kotaku]] |date=14 June 2013 |access-date=21 August 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130820080218/http://www.kotaku.com.au/2013/06/the-new-mad-max-game-looks-great-but/ |archive-date=20 August 2013 |url-status=usurped }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://au.ign.com/articles/2013/07/02/avalanche-mad-max-will-have-australian-accent-after-all |title=Avalanche: Mad Max Will Have Australian Accent After All |last=Dyer |first=Mitch |work=[[IGN]]|date=3 July 2013 |access-date=3 July 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160721025844/http://au.ign.com/articles/2013/07/02/avalanche-mad-max-will-have-australian-accent-after-all |archive-date=21 July 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref> Australian actor [[Bren Foster]] was subsequently chosen for the role.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://kotaku.com/two-very-australian-things-the-mad-max-video-game-got-r-1729485137|title=Two Very Australian Things The Mad Max Video Game Got Right|first=Luke|last=Plunkett|work=[[Kotaku]]|date=September 9, 2015|access-date=May 3, 2021}}</ref> Chumbucket, Max's mechanic and companion, is obsessed with the Magnum Opus; according to the game's lead writer, he "has a pseudo-religious/sexual relationship with engines".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/25/meet-the-weirdos-of-mad-max-s-wasteland.aspx?PostPageIndex=1|title=Meet The Weirdos Of Mad Max's Wasteland: Chumbucket|first=Jeff|last=Cork|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|date=25 March 2015|access-date=1 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150810190254/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/25/meet-the-weirdos-of-mad-max-s-wasteland.aspx?PostPageIndex=1|archive-date=10 August 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Scabrous Scrotus, the game's main antagonist, is a warlord designed as a "bloodthirsty monster that only can find solace from his own pain through the suffering of others".<ref name="GI characters"/> Enemies' faces are painted and scarred; according to game director Frank Rooke, their appearance "is kind of the approach of how this civilization merged into this kind of state".<ref name="GI characters">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/25/meet-the-weirdos-of-mad-max-s-wasteland.aspx?PostPageIndex=4|title=Meet The Weirdos Of Mad Max's Wasteland: Scrotus' Minions|first=Jeff|last=Cork|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|date=25 March 2015|access-date=1 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150703075114/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/25/meet-the-weirdos-of-mad-max-s-wasteland.aspx?PostPageIndex=4|archive-date=3 July 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Like the films, the game does not identify the apocalypse; its developers wanted to give "a sense of mystery" to the wasteland so players could imagine how the wasteland evolved.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.polygon.com/2013/12/4/5174312/mad-max-maintaining-sense-of-mystery-game-world|title=Mad Max devs on maintaining the game world's 'sense of mystery'|first=Samit|last=Sarker|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=4 December 2013|access-date=1 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150702022433/http://www.polygon.com/2013/12/4/5174312/mad-max-maintaining-sense-of-mystery-game-world|archive-date=2 July 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> The game's setting is described as "wasteland creole", with elements of a number of civilizations, so its characters have a variety of accents.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/11/where-is-mad-max-s-wasteland-and-does-it-fit-with-the-films.aspx|title=Where Is Mad Max's Wasteland, And Does It Fit With The Films?|first=Jeff|last=Cork|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|date=11 March 2015|access-date=30 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150628210935/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/03/11/where-is-mad-max-s-wasteland-and-does-it-fit-with-the-films.aspx|archive-date=28 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

Lead designer Emil Krafting said that gameplay was the top priority during development. Like the [[Just Cause (video game series)|''Just Cause'' series]], the developer aimed to give players autonomy by providing tools to create their own events.<ref name="IGN">{{cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2013/10/29/mad-max-not-looking-for-inspiration-from-fallout-rage-or-borderlands|title=Mad Max Not Looking for Inspiration From Fallout, Rage Or Borderlands|first=Luke|last=Reilly|work=[[IGN]]|date=28 October 2015|access-date=1 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150528122921/http://www.ign.com/articles/2013/10/29/mad-max-not-looking-for-inspiration-from-fallout-rage-or-borderlands|archive-date=28 May 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> The studios intended to build a dynamic world, creating "a seamless series of events".<ref name="GRadar"/> The game was inspired by the atmosphere of the ''Mad Max'' universe, rather than a particular film in the series. They were not influenced by other post-apocalyptic video games such as ''[[Fallout (franchise)|Fallout]]'', ''[[Rage (video game)|Rage]]'', and ''[[Borderlands (series)|Borderlands]]'' since most of those games were inspired by the original ''[[Mad Max]]''.<ref name="Poly sources"/> The company said that the game's vehicular combat posed a challenge because of their inexperience with that type of game.<ref name="Poly sources"/> The car customization system was designed to give players more freedom.<ref name="VG247Graphics"/> Garages allowing players to upgrade and repair their cars were originally intended to be featured in the game. The idea was later scrapped, since the studio thought the element "interfered with gameplay".<ref name="IGN Gameplay 1"/>

[[File:Mad Max development.jpg|thumb|alt=Screenshot of Max, the Magnum Opus and a large ship half-buried in sand|Regions feature different landmarks to create a variety of environments. The developers used vibrant colors to depict the sky in contrast to the brown ground.|left]]
The game's world was inspired by the ''Just Cause'' series, which features large [[sandbox games|sandboxes]] for players to explore. One challenge faced by the developers was building a wasteland with a variety of environments, since ''Mad Max'' is Avalanche's first post-apocalyptic game.<ref name="Poly sources"/> They spent most of their time designing ground and terrain variations to minimize repetition in the landscape.<ref name="VentureBeat1"/> The game world is scaled according to gameplay density and frequency; the development team emphasized creating a world with choices and distractions, rather than focusing on size.<ref name="VentureBeat1"/> According to design director Magnus Nedfors, the game world was designed to be barren, threatening, and hostile, while also offering "high-octane, full speed ahead, full of action moments" as well as “moments of solitude" whereas players in take in the surroundings and relax. Sundberg hoped that players would compare ''Mad Max''{{'}}s desert setting to the western setting of ''[[Red Dead Redemption]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/2015/05/26/mad-max-video-game-reveals-a-desert-full-of-danger-hands-on-preview/|title=Mad Max video game reveals a desert full of danger (hands-on preview)|first=Dean|last=Takahashi|work=[[VentureBeat]]|date=26 May 2015|access-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150617033512/http://venturebeat.com/2015/05/26/mad-max-video-game-reveals-a-desert-full-of-danger-hands-on-preview/|archive-date=17 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Since the game is set in a desert, the team used vibrant colors for the sky.<ref name="Gematsu">{{cite web|url=http://gematsu.com/2013/08/interview-avalanches-john-fuller-on-mad-max|title=Interview: Avalanche's John Fuller On Mad Max|first=Roland|last=Gmyrek|work=Gematsu|date=27 August 2013|access-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623144435/http://gematsu.com/2013/08/interview-avalanches-john-fuller-on-mad-max|archive-date=23 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Mad Max'' is powered by Apex Engine (formerly known as Avalanche Engine), an in-house proprietary engine.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.develop-online.net/interview/from-just-cause-to-mad-max-avalanche-ten-years-on/0184618|title=From Just Cause to Mad Max – Avalanche ten years on|first=Will|last=Freeman|magazine=Develop|date=17 October 2013|access-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150704151721/http://www.develop-online.net/interview/from-just-cause-to-mad-max-avalanche-ten-years-on/0184618|archive-date=4 July 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> The team introduced new graphical features to the engine during the development of ''Mad Max''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dsogaming.com/interviews/avalanche-on-avalanche-engines-future-tech-features-dx12-dynamic-tessellation-plans/|title=Avalanche on Avalanche Engine's Future, Tech Features, DX12 & Dynamic Tessellation Plans|first=John|last=Papadopoulos|work=Dark Side of Gaming|date=10 May 2015|access-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923220711/http://www.dsogaming.com/interviews/avalanche-on-avalanche-engines-future-tech-features-dx12-dynamic-tessellation-plans/|archive-date=23 September 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> The team also worked on improving the world's [[draw distance]] and ensured that gameplay across the three major platforms have no significant difference.<ref name="VG247Graphics">{{cite web|url=https://www.vg247.com/2013/09/02/mad-max-an-open-world-destruction-derby-of-pain/|title=Mad Max: an open world destruction derby of pain – interview|first=Dave|last=Cook|work=[[VG247]]|date=2 September 2013|access-date=21 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920153241/https://www.vg247.com/2013/09/02/mad-max-an-open-world-destruction-derby-of-pain/|archive-date=20 September 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Release and marketing==
[[File:Mad Max (20363799085).jpg|thumb|Promotion at [[Gamescom]] 2015]]

On 14 February 2013, a blurry screenshot of the game was released by Sundberg.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pcgamer.com/avalanch/|title=Just Cause creators tease new project with blurry shot of [[Sony]]'s press conference, with a scheduled 2014 release for [[PlayStation 3]], [[PlayStation 4]], [[Windows]], [[Xbox 360]], and [[Xbox One]].<ref name="gs-mad_max-announce">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/mad-max-out-for-next-gen-consoles-in-2014/1100-6409696/|title=Mad Max out for next-gen consoles in 2014|last=Leo|first=Jon|publisher=[[GameSpot]]|date=10 June 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> In April 2014, Avalanche announced that ''Mad Max'' would be delayed until the following year,<ref>{{cite (website)|Polygon]]|date=25 April 2014|access-date=17 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150217073032/http://www.polygon.com/2014/4/25/5652488/mad-max-trailer|archive-date=17
