''Mad Max'' received "mixed or average" reviews from critics, according to review aggregator [[Metacritic]].<ref name="MCPC" /><ref name="MCXONE" /><ref name="MCPS4" /> George Miller said in a 2024 interview that the game "wasn't as good as" how he wanted it to be.<ref>{{cite web |last=Byrd |first=Matthew |date=23 May 2024 |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/games/why-george-miller-doesnt-like-the-only-good-mad-max-video-game/ |title=Why George Miller Doesn't Like the Only Good Mad Max Video Game |work=[[Den of Geek]] |access-date=1 May 2024 }}</ref> Retrospectively, the game was considered to be "underrated".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/mad-max-developer-hits-back-at-film-director-george-miller-after-claim-game-wasnt-as-good-as-he-wanted-it-to-be|title=Mad Max developer hits back at film director George Miller after claim game "wasn't as good as [he] wanted it to be"|first=Ed|last=Nightingale|work=[[Eurogamer]]|date=May 24, 2024|accessdate=May 27, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.redbull.com/ca-en/most-underrated-games-of-the-decade|title=The 10 most criminally overlooked games of the decade|first=Joe|last=Ellison|work=[[Red Bull]]|date=September 1, 2020|accessdate=May 27, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/mad-max-george-miller-wants-hideo-kojima-to-make-video-game-adaptation|title=Mad Max Director George Miller Would Like Hideo Kojima to Make a Video Game Adaptation|first=Adele|last=Ankers-Range|work=[[IGN]]|date=May 23, 2024|accessdate=May 27, 2024}}</ref>

Its story received a mixed response. Brandin Tyrrel of ''[[IGN]]'' found the story surprising and genuine, despite most of the action occurring later in the game. Tyrrel wrote that the characters have different personalities and distinct qualities, and considered them the "true star" of the game.<ref name="IGNRev"/> According to Chris Carter of ''[[Destructoid]]'', the game's story engages the player.<ref name="Destruct"/> Leon Hurley of ''[[GamesRadar]]'' found the overall story weak and "barely exist[ing] for the majority of the game", but thought the game's climax was exciting.<ref name="GRadarRev"/> Matt Bertz of ''[[Game Informer]]'' also criticized the story, calling it thin and light, and called the voice actors' performances uneven.<ref name="GI"/>

''Mad Max''{{'}}s world design received generally positive reviews. According to Brandin Tyrrel, it captured the films' savage tone and the game's sandbox was a "gorgeous" setting for players to explore.<ref name="IGNRev"/> GamesRadar's Leon Hurley praised the game's scale, which he compared to ''[[The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt]]''.<ref name="GRadarRev"/> Martin Robinson of ''[[Eurogamer]]'' compared its scale favorably to Avalanche's previous ''[[Just Cause (video game series)|Just Cause]]'' game series, and opined that Avalanche had successfully combined the ''Mad Max'' universe with an open-world game design.<ref name="EuroG"/> Matt Bertz praised the game's inhospitable atmosphere, commending Avalanche for adding a variety of styles and a vibrant sky to an otherwise-boring sandbox. Daniel Bloodworth of ''[[GameTrailers]]'' echoed Bertz, calling each region unique and distinct. Bloodworth also praised Avalanche for its efforts in crafting the world. Peter Brown of ''[[GameSpot]]'' praised ''Mad Max''{{'}}s natural disasters, writing that it set a new standard for in-game weather effects.<ref name="GSpot"/> Philip Kollar of ''[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]'' criticized the game's layout, writing that every location in the game feels identical and its bland environments discourage exploration.<ref name="Poly"/>

Tyrrel considered the vehicular combat one of the game's best elements, adding a layer of creativity. Brown praised the car action, calling it intense, complex, and unpredictable, but criticized the over-simplistic and shallow on-foot combat.<ref name="GSpot"/> Carter compared the game's vehicular controls to the best racing games, and commended its handling. He also praised the car mechanics, writing that it has offered players a cinematic experience.<ref name="Destruct"/> Tyrrel liked the additions to the game's combat (such as the introduction of weapons and the Fury mode), writing that they added depth to the combat.<ref name="IGNRev"/> Hurley praised the game's progression system, which he found satisfying, and the balance between vehicular and on-foot combat.<ref name="GRadarRev"/> Bloodworth wrote that the melee combat used a "tried-and-true system" which worked well, despite awkward camera angles. Kollar criticized the boss fights, which he thought lacked variety.<ref name="Poly"/>

Other gameplay aspects received mixed reviews. Tyrrel praised the customization system for Max and the Magnum Opus, since the customization impacts the gameplay and makes the overall experience more rewarding;<ref name="IGNRev"/> Kollar echoed this.<ref name="Poly"/> Brown criticized the game for failing to offer much challenge or a sense of accomplishment to players. He called the health system a redundant addition in which resources, such as water and food, play an insignificant role and can be neglected by players. Brown also criticized the scrap-collecting system, writing that it frustrated most players and slowed the game's pace.<ref name="GSpot"/> However, Robinson wrote that those elements reflect the barbarian nature of the wasteland. He praised its world design (which he thought echoed the films), describing it as "a world of twisted metal and sudden violence that's there to be survived rather than conquered".<ref name="EuroG"/> Bloodworth criticized the game's stronghold system, which he called repetitive. Bertz criticized the game's lack of a climbing system, which hinders movement;<ref name="GI"/> this was echoed by Carter.<ref name="Destruct"/>

''Mad Max''{{'}}s quest design also received mixed reviews. Tyrrel praised the content and activities scattered across the world, calling the activities engaging for most players. However, he disliked the repetition which dragged down their [[replay value]].<ref name="IGNRev"/> Hurley found it easy for players to become confused in the game's early stages, since the objectives are unclear.<ref name="GRadarRev"/> Brown criticized the structure of several quests which force players to use a certain method, removing freedom and creativity.<ref name="GSpot"/> Chris Carter of ''[[Destructoid]]'' wrote that the game brought nothing new to the genre, and its quests and features were too similar to typical [[Ubisoft]] open-world design.<ref name="Destruct"/>

The game had some technical problems when it was released. Tyrrel noted an unstable [[frame rate]] and occasional texture pop-up,<ref name="IGNRev"/> and Kollar identified audio problems.<ref name="Poly"/>

===Sales===
''Mad Max'' was the second-best selling game in the United Kingdom in its first week of release on the United Kingdom software retail chart, only behind ''[[Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain]]'', which was released the same day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.videogamer.com/ps4/mad_max/news/uk_video_game_charts_metal_gear_solid_5_the_phantom_pain_beats_mad_max_to_the_uk_no_1.html|title=UK Video Game Charts: Metal Gear Solid 5: The Phantom Pain beats Mad Max to the UK No.1|first=James|last=Orry|work=VideoGamer.com|date=7 September 2015|access-date=7 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304085257/http://www.videogamer.com/ps4/mad_max/news/uk_video_game_charts_metal_gear_solid_5_the_phantom_pain_beats_mad_max_to_the_uk_no_1.html|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> According to the [[NPD Group]], it was the eighth-best selling game in the United States in September 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/2015/10/19/september-2015-npd-ps4-wins/|title=September 2015 NPD: NBA, NFL games have big month as hardware sputters|first=Jeff|last=Grubb|work=[[VentureBeat]]|date=19 October 2015|access-date=24 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151023110336/http://venturebeat.com/2015/10/19/september-2015-npd-ps4-wins/|archive-date=23 October 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

Former Avalanche CEO Christofer Sundberg revealed in 2024 that "[WB] blamed us for the bad sales" and that canceled DLC was "just sitting there waiting to be released". Sundberg attributed the game's commercial underperformance to being released on the same day as ''Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain'', and his attempts at convincing Warner Bros. to move the game's release date were unsuccessful.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/george-miller-criticizes-2015s-mad-max-game-developer-responds-with-heated-messages/1100-6523661/|title=George Miller Criticizes 2015's Mad Max Game, Developer Responds With Heated Messages |first=Eddie |last=Makuch |work=[[GameSpot]] |date=23 May 2024 |access-date=28 May 2024 }}</ref>

'''''Manhunt''''' is a 2003 [[stealth game]] developed by [[Rockstar North]] and published by [[Rockstar Games]]. It was released for the [[PlayStation 2]] in November 2003, followed by [[Microsoft Windows]] and [[Xbox (console)|Xbox]] releases in April 2004.<ref name="ign">{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2003/11/18/manhunt-2 |title=Manhunt (PS2) |author=Perry, Douglass C. |date=November 18, 2003 |website=[[IGN]] |publisher=[[Ziff Davis]] |access-date=August 31, 2019 |archive-date=August 26, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190826015113/https://www.ign.com/articles/2003/11/18/manhunt-2 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/12130/Manhunt/ |title=Manhunt |website=[[Steam (service)|Steam]] |publisher=[[Valve Corporation|Valve]] |access-date=August 31, 2019 |archive-date=August 31, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190831150355/https://store.steampowered.com/app/12130/Manhunt/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Set within the fictional Carcer City, players control a [[death row]] inmate named James Earl Cash, who is forced to participate in a series of [[snuff film]]s by killing criminal gang members sent to hunt him on camera.

The game received positive reviews from critics, with praise towards its dark tone and violent gameplay, although the combat and level design were criticized. Due to its graphic violence, ''Manhunt'' was the subject of significant [[Video game controversies|controversy]] and banned in several countries. It was also implicated in a murder by the UK media, although this accusation was later rejected by the police and courts. While not a commercial hit, ''Manhunt'' developed a substantial [[cult following]] and was followed by a stand-alone sequel, ''[[Manhunt 2]]'', in 2007. The PlayStation 2 version of the game was re-released through the [[PlayStation Network]] for the [[PlayStation 3]] in 2013 and [[PlayStation 4]] in 2016, and the [[Xbox]] version was re-released in 2021 through the [[List of backward-compatible games for Xbox One and Series X/S|Xbox Backwards Compatibility]] program.

==Gameplay==
[[File:Manhunt stealth.jpg|thumb|left|An example of stealth in ''Manhunt''; Cash hides in the shadows from a hunter, preparing to sneak up on him.]]
''Manhunt'' is a [[stealth game]] played from a [[Third-person (video games)|third-person perspective]]. The game consists of twenty levels, called "scenes", as well as four unlockable bonus scenes.<ref name="ign"/> Players survive the scenes by dispatching enemy gang members, occasionally with [[firearm]]s, but primarily by stealthily executing them.<ref name="IGNbasics">{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/wikis/manhunt/Basics |title=Manhunt: Basics |website=IGN |date=March 28, 2012 |publisher=Ziff Davis |access-date=January 16, 2020 |archive-date=August 15, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200815001105/https://www.ign.com/wikis/manhunt/Basics |url-status=live }}</ref> At the end of each scene, players are graded based on their performance, and awarded one to five stars. Unlockable content becomes available when the player achieves three or more stars on a certain number of levels. On normal difficulty (called "Fetish"), players can earn only four stars; one is awarded for completing the scene under a certain amount of time, and one to three stars are awarded based on the brutality of the executions carried out during the scene. On hard difficulty (called "Hardcore"), players are graded out of five stars; one for speed, one to three for brutality and one for completing the scene. To gain the maximum number of stars, a set number of brutal executions must be carried out over the course of each scene; face-to-face fighting does not award stars.<ref name="IGNbasics"/>

To carry out executions, players must approach a hunter from behind, undetected. To facilitate this, each scene is full of "dark spots", shadows where the player can hide. Enemies cannot see into the shadows, unless they see the player actually entering the area. A standard technique in the game is to hide in the shadows and tap a wall to attract the attention of a nearby hunter. When the hunter has examined the area and is moving away, players can easily ambush and execute them.<ref name="gspot">{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/manhunt-review/1900-6083971/ |title=Manhunt Review (PS2) |author=Kasavin, Greg |date=November 19, 2003 |website=[[GameSpot]] |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |access-date=January 16, 2020 |archive-date=January 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113093225/https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/manhunt-review/1900-6083971/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The game has three levels of execution, with each level progressively more violent and graphic than the last: "hasty" executions are quick and not very bloody, "violent" are considerably more gory, and "gruesome" are over-the-top blood-soaked murders. Players are in control of which level they use; once players have locked onto an enemy, the lock-on reticule changes color over time to indicate the three levels: white, yellow and red.<ref name="1up">{{cite web |url=http://www.1up.com/reviews/manhunt_3 |title=Manhunt (PS2) |author=Smith, David |date=May 9, 2004 |website=[[1UP.com]] |publisher=Ziff Davis |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160312194301/http://www.1up.com/reviews/manhunt_3 |archive-date=March 12, 2016 |url-status=dead |access-date=January 16, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gamechronicles.com/reviews/ps2/manhunt/manhunt.htm |title=Manhunt (PS2) |author=Smith, Mark |date=February 2, 2004 |website=Game Chronicles |access-date=February 27, 2007 |archive-date=February 10, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120210065719/http://www.gamechronicles.com/reviews/ps2/manhunt/manhunt.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Over the course of the game, players can use a wide variety of weapons, including [[Plastic bag|plastic bags]], [[Baseball bat|baseball bats]], [[Crowbar|crowbars]] and a variety of [[Edged weapon|bladed items]]. Later in the game firearms are available for use when executions become impractical. Should players take damage, their health depletes; health can be restored through the use of painkillers, which are available throughout each scene.<ref name="gspot"/> Players have a stamina meter which depletes as they sprint, but automatically replenishes when remaining stationary.<ref name="IGNbasics"/> ''Manhunt'' makes use of the PlayStation 2's optional [[Universal Serial Bus|USB]] Microphone and the [[Xbox Live]] [[microphone]] feature on the Xbox in their respective versions of the game. When such a device is connected, players can use the sound of their own voice to distract in-game enemies and hear director's command through the Headset directly. This adds an extra element to the stealth aspect and immersion of the game, as players must refrain from making noises such as coughing as these sounds too can attract the attention of any nearby hunters.<ref name="IGNbasics"/>

==Synopsis==
===Setting===
''Manhunt'' is set in the fictional Carcer City, a dilapidated [[Rust Belt|rust belt]] city rife with corruption and crime.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2012-08-12-retrospective-manhunt|title=Retrospective: Manhunt|work=[[Eurogamer]]|publisher=[[Gamer Network]]|first=Jon|last=Denton|date=August 12, 2012|access-date=August 30, 2020|archive-date=October 30, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201030201923/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2012-08-12-retrospective-manhunt|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2004/TECH/fun.games/05/28/review.manhunt/|title=Review: 'Manhunt' raises video game violence bar|publisher=[[CNN]]|first=Marc|last=Saltzman|date=June 1, 2004|access-date=August 30, 2020|archive-date=October 29, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201029165706/http://edition.cnn.com/2004/TECH/fun.games/05/28/review.manhunt/|url-status=live}}</ref> On the prowl around the city are numerous violent gangs, who seek to find and kill the player.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/04/06/the-gangs-of-manhunt|title=The Gangs of Manhunt|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=[[Ziff Davis]]|first=Douglass C.|last=Perry|date=April 7, 2004|access-date=August 30, 2020|archive-date=October 21, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021025905/https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/04/06/the-gangs-of-manhunt|url-status=live}}</ref> The game is set in a [[shared universe]] with the ''[[Grand Theft Auto]]'' series.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Jacked The Outlaw Story of Grand Theft Auto|author=David Kushner|date=April 3, 2012|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=978-0470936375}}</ref>

===Plot===
In 2003 in Carcer City, a journalist (Kate Miller<ref name="TTI-MANUAL"/>) reports about James Earl Cash (Stephen Wilfong<ref name="TTI-MANUAL"/>), a [[death row]] inmate who has been recently executed by [[lethal injection]]. However, Cash was only [[Sedative|sedated]], and awakens to an unknown voice referring to himself as "The Director" ([[Brian Cox (actor)|Brian Cox]]<ref name="TTI-MANUAL"/>), who gives him instructions through an earpiece. The Director promises Cash his freedom, but only if he kills "Hunters" – gang members sent to hunt him – in special areas around Carcer City filmed by [[Closed-circuit television|CCTV]]. Cash is first pitted against the Hoods, a gang of dangerous criminals and corrupt police officers patrolling an abandoned area of the city. After eliminating them, he is abducted by the Cerberus, the Director's personal security unit, who take him to another part of Carcer City.

While the Director monitors his actions, Cash is forced to kill more criminals across various abandoned locations, including a [[white power skinhead]] gang called the Skinz, a sadistic paramilitary group called the Wardogs, an outlaw gang called the Innocentz (consisting of the Skullyz, mostly made up of Hispanic occultists, and the Babyfaces, a group of [[Pedophilia|pedophiles]] and mentally challenged murderers), and a gang of former asylum inmates called the Smileys. Eventually, the Director betrays Cash and, after ordering the deaths of his family members, whom he had abducted, tries to murder Cash as part of his film's climax. Cash survives the trap, and escapes after vowing revenge on the Director.

The remaining Wardogs, led by the Director's right-hand man Ramirez (Chris McKinney<ref name="TTI-MANUAL"/>), are sent to re-capture Cash, and they manage to trap him in a game of [[cat and mouse]]. Cash prevails and kills Ramirez and his men, before being found by the journalist reporting on him, who reveals that the Director is Lionel Starkweather, a former film producer from [[Los Santos (Grand Theft Auto)|Los Santos]] who now produces for a [[snuff film]] ring. The journalist has acquired enough evidence against Starkweather to get him convicted, but needs Cash to escort her to her apartment to retrieve it. Meanwhile, Starkweather blackmails corrupt police chief Gary Schaffer into sending his men to kill Cash and the journalist, but the two manage to avoid them. After retrieving the evidence, Cash tells the journalist to leave the city with it while he goes after Starkweather.

Pursued by the police and [[SWAT]] throughout the subway and streets, Cash is eventually cornered in a train yard and almost executed. He is saved by the Cerberus, who kill the SWAT team and take Cash to Starkweather's mansion so they can execute him themselves. Cash escapes after the Cerberus are distracted when Piggsy (Hunter Platin<ref name="TTI-MANUAL"/>), a chainsaw-wielding maniac that Starkweather has kept chained up in the attic, suddenly breaks free. Heading to the mansion's upper levels, Cash uses stealth attacks to fight Piggsy and tricks him into standing on a grate, which collapses under his weight, allowing Cash to take Piggsy's [[chainsaw]] and kill him with it. After eliminating the remaining Cerberus, Cash confronts Starkweather in his office and murders him with the chainsaw. The media and police arrive at the mansion as the journalist exposes Starkweather's snuff ring and police complicity, leading to Schaffer being criminally prosecuted for corruption. Cash, however, is nowhere to be found.

==Development==
[[Rockstar North]] began development of ''Manhunt'' in 2000, building the game with the [[RenderWare]] engine that had been used for the ''Grand Theft Auto'' titles.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2003/08/22/manhunt-3 |title=Manhunt (Preview) |author=Perry, Douglass C. |date=August 22, 2003 |website=IGN |publisher=Ziff Davis |access-date=January 16, 2020 |archive-date=July 14, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190714012111/https://www.ign.com/articles/2003/08/22/manhunt-3 |url-status=live }}</ref> In September 2003, ''[[GamesMaster (magazine)|GamesMaster]]'' published a preview of ''Manhunt'', commenting "[Rockstar North has] scraped its imagination to further twist the way games are made in the future and delivers a chiseled, no-apologies assault on gaming standards. [...] it possesses a warped subtlety that questions game reality... It creates a barren, harsh, violent experience and then punctures it with something trippy and darkly comic..."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rockstargames.com/manhunt/txt/news.txt|title=Manhunt Out Now for Xbox, PC and PlayStation 2|work=[[Rockstar Games]]|access-date=August 15, 2020|archive-date=October 30, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201030082551/https://www.rockstargames.com/manhunt/txt/news.txt|url-status=live}}</ref> In a retrospective piece, a former Rockstar employee admitted that the game almost caused a [[mutiny]] in the company, saying that the team had "already weathered plenty of controversy over ''[[Grand Theft Auto III|GTA III]]'' and ''[[Grand Theft Auto: Vice City|Vice City]]''—we were no strangers to it—but ''Manhunt'' felt different. With ''GTA'', we always had the excuse that the gameplay was untethered—you never had to hurt anybody that wasn't a "bad guy" in one of the missions. You could play completely ethically if you wanted, and the game was parody anyway, so lighten up".<ref name="GRadar+">{{cite web |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/manhunt-nearly-caused-a-mutiny-at-rockstar/ |title=Manhunt nearly caused a "mutiny" at Rockstar |author=Cundy, Matt |date=July 26, 2007 |website=[[GamesRadar+]] |publisher=[[Future plc]] |access-date=March 29, 2013 |archive-date=October 6, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121006015432/http://www.gamesradar.com/manhunt-nearly-caused-a-mutiny-at-rockstar/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

''Manhunt'' was announced at [[E3]] in May 2003.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2003/05/14/e3-2003-manhunt-ps2-bound|title=E3 2003: Manhunt PS2 Bound|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=[[Ziff Davis]]|author=IGN Staff|date=May 14, 2003|access-date=August 26, 2020|archive-date=October 28, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201028010903/https://www.ign.com/articles/2003/05/14/e3-2003-manhunt-ps2-bound|url-status=live}}</ref> The game was originally slated for an October release date,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/manhunt-and-max-payne-2-due-in-october|title=Manhunt and Max Payne 2 due in October|work=[[Gamesindustry.biz]]|publisher=[[Gamer Network]]|first=Kristan|last=Reed|date=August 14, 2003|access-date=August 26, 2020|archive-date=October 26, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201026132532/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/manhunt-and-max-payne-2-due-in-october|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Previews"/> and it was eventually released for the [[PlayStation 2]] on November 19, 2003, in North America, followed by a European release on November 21.<ref>{{cite press release |url=http://ir.take2games.com/releasedetail.cfm?releaseid=131241 |title=Rockstar Games Ships Manhunt for PlayStation®2 |publisher=[[Take-Two Interactive]] |date=November 19, 2003 |archive-date=August 19, 2004 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040819204922/http://ir.take2games.com/releasedetail.cfm?releaseid=131241 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/rockstar-ships-manhunt/1100-6083913/|title=Rockstar ships Manhunt|work=[[GameSpot]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|first=Justin|last=Calvert|date=November 20, The PlayStation 2 and PC versions of ''Manhunt'' received "generally favorable reviews", while the Xbox version received "mixed or average" reviews, according to the [[Review aggregator|review aggregation]] website [[Metacritic]].<ref name="metapc"/><ref name="metaps2"/><ref name="metaxbox"/> As of March 26, 2008, the ''Manhunt'' series has sold 1.7 million copies worldwide.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://taketwovalue.com/documents/TTWO_Value.pdf#page=15 |title=Recommendation of the Board of Directors to Reject Electronic Arts Inc.'s Tender Offer |date=March 26, 2008 |website=[[Take-Two Interactive]] |page=15 |format=PDF |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080408234728/http://taketwovalue.com/documents/TTWO_Value.pdf#page=15 |archive-date=April 8, 2008 |url-status=dead |access-date=April 21, 2008}}</ref> At the [[7th Annual Interactive Achievement Awards]], the game was nominated for "[[D.I.C.E. Award for Action Game of the Year|Console Action/Adventure Game of the Year]]".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.escmag.com/cgi-bin/archives.cgi?category=1&view=1.14.04-2.13.04 |title=7th Annual Interactive Achievement Awards Nominees |author=Becker, Erich |website=ESCMag |date=February 13, 2004 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061114065139/http://www.escmag.com/cgi-bin/archives.cgi?category=1&view=1.14.04-2.13.04 |archive-date=November 14, 2006 |url-status=dead |access-date=February 27, 2007}}</ref> ''Manhunt'' received a "Gold" sales award from the [[The Association for UK Interactive Entertainment|Entertainment and Leisure Software Publishers Association]] (ELSPA),<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.elspa.com/?i=3943 |title=ELSPA Sales Awards: Gold |website=[[The Association for UK Interactive Entertainment|Entertainment and Leisure Software Publishers Association]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090319031650/http://www.elspa.com/?i=3943 |archive-date=March 19, 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> indicating sales of at least 200,000 copies in the United Kingdom.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/112220/ELSPA_Wii_Fit_Mario_Kart_Reach_Diamond_Status_In_UK.php |title=ELSPA: Wii Fit, Mario Kart Reach Diamond Status In UK |author=Caoili, Eric |date=November 26, 2008 |website=[[Gamasutra]] |publisher=[[UBM plc]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170918063107/https://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/112220/ELSPA_Wii_Fit_Mario_Kart_Reach_Diamond_Status_In_UK.php |archive-date=September 18, 2017 |url-status=dead |access-date=September 19, 2017 }}</ref>

The game's dark [[Nihilism|nihilistic]] tone and violent nature were singled out by many critics as representing something unique in the world of video gaming. ''[[GameSpot]]'' concluded that, "like it or not, the game pushes the envelope of video game violence and shows you countless scenes of wholly uncensored, heavily stylized carnage".<ref name="gspot"/> ''[[Game Informer]]'' praised the PS2 version's audacity and competent technical capabilities, stating "it's a frightening premise that places gamers in a psychological impasse. The crimes that you commit are unspeakable, yet the gameplay that leads to these horrendous acts is so polished and fierce that it's thrilling."<ref name="gameinformer"/> ''[[IGN]]'' complimented the same console version's overall challenge, calling it a "solid, deep experience for seasoned gamers pining for some hardcore, challenging games".<ref name="ign"/> ''[[Edge (magazine)|Edge]]'' gave the same console version eight out of ten, saying, "Like ''[[Grand Theft Auto|GTA]]'' there's more to this than shock and awe. Within its linear structure there is a lot of freedom within which to act, much more so than both ''[[Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell (video game)|Splinter Cell]]'' and ''[[Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty|Metal Gear Solid 2]]'', the titles which ''Manhunt'' most closely resembles."<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://www.edge-online.com/review/manhunt-review/ |title=Manhunt Review (PS2) |author=Edge staff |magazine=[[Edge (magazine)|Edge]] |publisher=Future plc |issue=132 |date=January 2004 |page=96 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130403115856/http://www.edge-online.com/review/manhunt-review/ |archive-date=April 3, 2013 |url-status=dead |access-date=January 16, 2020}}</ref>

''[[Toronto Star]]'' writer [[Ben Rayner]], praised the relevance of the game, defending its violence and graphic nature as very much a product of its time, and condemning calls to have it banned; 
<blockquote>
As entertainment and cultural artefact, ''Manhunt'' is totally disturbing. But so is the evening news, the "I'll eat anything for money" lunacy of ''[[Fear Factor]]'' and the unfettered, misanthropic gunplay of ''[[Bad Boys II]]'', so I will defend until my last breath Rockstar's right to sell this stuff to me and anyone else who wants it. ... Do I think games such as these could have dire psychological consequences, particularly for young people? As always, I remain agnostic on the matter. Who knows, really? The debate will never be resolved. The American military obviously thinks there's something there: The troubling new TV ad campaign for the U.S. reserves lures potential young soldiers with tales of adventure accompanied by blatant, video-game-styled animation. And, curiously, no one has complained about or tried to ban ''[[SOCOM U.S. Navy SEALs]]'', in which stealth and killing figure even more heavily than in ''Manhunt''.<ref>{{cite news |title=In my private moments, I'm a murderer |author=Rayner, Ben |author-link=Ben Rayner |date=January 25, 2004 |newspaper=[[Toronto Star]] |publisher=[[Torstar]]}}</ref>
</blockquote>

The ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'' was especially complimentary of the game, arguing that it marked a significant moment in video gaming history;
<blockquote>
''Manhunt'' is easily the most violent game ever made. It will likely be dismissed by many as a disgusting murder simulator with no reason to exist. But ''Manhunt'' also is the ''[[A Clockwork Orange (film)|Clockwork Orange]]'' of video games, holding your eyes open so as to not miss a single splatter – asking you, is this really what you enjoy watching? Had ''Manhunt'' been poorly made, using the snuff film angle as a cheap gimmick, the game would have been shameful and exploitative. What elevates it to a grotesque, chilling work of art is both presentation and game play. ''Manhunt'' is solid as a game; it's engaging to use stealth as you creep through the streets of this wicked city, using your smarts to avoid death, while dishing out much of your own. If ''Manhunt'' succeeds at retail, it will say more about America's fascination with violence than any political discourse or social debate. That makes ''Manhunt'' the most important video game of the last five years.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-2003-11-24-0311240161-story.html |title=Manhunt a solid game, but do you want the gore? |author=Buchanan, Levi |date=November 24, 2003 |newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]] |publisher=[[Tribune Publishing]] |access-date=January 16, 2020 |archive-date=April 30, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200430033223/https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-2003-11-24-0311240161-story.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
</blockquote>

The game received some criticism. Certain gameplay elements, such as the shooting mechanics, were called "frustrating" by ''[[Eurogamer]]'', who claimed that "more than half the time the targeting reticule refuses to acknowledge an oncoming enemy until they're virtually in front of you."<ref name="eurog"/> ''GameSpot'' concurred, noting that the "[[Artificial intelligence|AI]] is much worse in the more action-oriented levels".<ref name="gspot"/> ''[[1UP.com]]'' said that one quickly became "tired of [the] violence ... AI quirks [and] repetitive level design."<ref name="1up"/>

==Controversy==
[[File:Mahuntstyle.jpg|thumb|''Manhunt'' attracted controversy due to its graphic execution scenes. In this particular execution, Cash suffocates an enemy with a plastic bag.]]
The controversy surrounding the game stems primarily from the graphic manner in which the player executes enemies. In 2007, former Rockstar employee Jeff Williams revealed that even the game's staff were somewhat uncomfortable about the level of violence; "there was almost a mutiny at the company over that game."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://badasscat.blogspot.com/2007/07/rockstar.html |title=Life During Wartime - Working at Rockstar Games |author=Williams, Jeff |date=July 24, 2007 |website=Alphabet City |publisher=[[BlogSpot]] |archive-url=https://archive.today/20070804084043/http://badasscat.blogspot.com/2007/07/rockstar.html |archive-date=August 4, 2007 |url-status=dead |access-date=September 2, 2010}}</ref> Williams explained that the game "just made us all feel icky. It was all about the violence, and it was realistic violence. We all knew there was no way we could explain away that game. There was no way to rationalize it. We were crossing a line."<ref name="GRadar+"/>

The violence in the game drew the attention of [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] [[Joe Baca]], who was the sponsor of a legislation to fine those who sell adult-themed games to players younger than 17. Baca said of ''Manhunt'', "it's telling kids how to kill someone, and it uses vicious, sadistic and cruel methods to kill".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-2003-11-24-0311240176-story.html |title='Manhunt,' the next step in video game violence |author=Gwinn, David |date=November 24, 2003 |newspaper=Chicago Tribune |publisher=Tribune Publishing |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130314111730/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2003-11-24/features/0311240176_1_gaming-scene-optional-headset-manhunt |archive-date=March 14, 2013 |url-status=live |access-date=January 16, 2020}}</ref> The media was drawn into the debate. For example, ''[[The Globe and Mail]]'' wrote "''Manhunt'' is a venal disconnect for the genre. There's no challenge, just assembly-line, ritualistic slaughter. It's less a video game and more a weapon of personal destruction. This is about stacking bodies. Perhaps the scariest fact of all: ''Manhunt'' is so user-friendly that any sharp 12-year-old could navigate through the entire game in one sitting."<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.thefreeradical.ca/videoGames/articlesOnManhunt.html |title=Belly up to the slaughter buffet |author=Ryan, Andrew |date=March 6, 2004 |newspaper=[[The Globe and Mail]] |publisher=[[The Woodbridge Company]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130323183148/http://www.thefreeradical.ca/videoGames/articlesOnManhunt.html |archive-date=March 23, 2013 |url-status=dead |access-date=November 8, 2012}}</ref>

===Murder of Stefan Pakeerah===
On July 28, 2004, the game was linked to the murder of 14-year-old Stefan Pakeerah by 17-year-old Warren Leblanc in [[Leicestershire]], England. Initial media reports claimed that police had found a copy of the game in Leblanc's bedroom. Giselle and Patrick Pakeerah, the victim's parents, claimed that the game had influenced LeBlanc and played a role in the murder.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Millward|first=David|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/1468088/Manhunt-computer-game-is-blamed-for-brutal-killing.html|title='Manhunt' computer game is blamed for brutal killing|journal=Daily Telegraph|date=July 28, 2004|access-date=March 31, 2020|language=en-GB|issn=0307-1235|archive-date=September 21, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200921111145/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/1468088/Manhunt-computer-game-is-blamed-for-brutal-killing.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/leicestershire/3934277.stm|title=Game blamed for hammer murder|date=July 29, 2004|access-date=March 31, 2020|language=en-GB|archive-date=May 21, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200521124723/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/leicestershire/3934277.stm|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/education/educationnews/4793981/Manhunt-computer-game-is-blamed-for-brutal-killing.html |title='Manhunt' computer game is blamed for brutal killing |author=Millward, David |date=July 29, 2004 |newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140520234948/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/education/educationnews/4793981/Manhunt-computer-game-is-blamed-for-brutal-killing.html |archive-date=May 20, 2014 |url-status=live |access-date=November 8, 2012}}</ref> The [[Video game content rating system|Entertainment and Leisure Software Publishers' Association]] (ELSPA) offered sympathy to the Pakeerah family but rejected any connection between the game and the murder. ELSPA also noted that the game was rated [[18 (British Board of Film Classification)|18]] by the [[British Board of Film Classification]] and was not intended for minors.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.totalvideogames.com/Manhunt/news/Manhunt-Blamed-for-Murder-5844.html |title='Manhunt' blamed for murder |author=Leyton, Chris |date=July 28, 2004 |website=TotalVideoGames |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130314113151/http://www.totalvideogames.com/Manhunt/news/Manhunt-Blamed-for-Murder-5844.html |archive-date=March 14, 2013 |url-status=dead |access-date=November 8, 2012}}</ref> Due to controversy, the game was removed from shelves by some vendors, including [[Game (retailer)|Game]] and [[Dixons Retail|Dixons]]. In response, Rockstar reiterated that it was intended for adults and denied any link to the murder.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/manhunt-blamed-for-uk-murder/1100-6103718/ |title=Manhunt blamed for UK murder |author=Thorsen, Tor |date=July 29, 2004 |website=GameSpot |publisher=CBS Interactive |access-date=January 16, 2020 |archive-date=April 30, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200430031450/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/manhunt-blamed-for-uk-murder/1100-6103718/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Media speculation of a potential ban on the game increased demand for it at physical and online retailers.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/leicestershire/3535268.stm |title=Manhunt game 'flying off shelves' |website=[[BBC News]] |publisher=[[BBC]] |date=August 4, 2004 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120828193442/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/leicestershire/3535268.stm |archive-date=August 28, 2012 |url-status=live |access-date=January 16, 2020}}</ref> Giselle Pakeerah stated her disappointment over the increased interest in the game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/manhunt-selling-out-in-uk/1100-6104220/ |title=Manhunt selling out in UK |author=Calvert, Justin |date=August 5, 2004 |website=GameSpot |publisher=CBS Interactive |access-date=January 16, 2020 |archive-date=December 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221206041446/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/manhunt-selling-out-in-uk/1100-6104220/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On July 30, 2004, American attorney [[Jack Thompson (activist)|Jack Thompson]], an advocate against violence in video games, claimed to have warned Rockstar prior to the game's release that it could inspire copycat killings.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://edition.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/europe/07/30/uk.manhunt.storeban/ |title=Retailer pulls 'murder' video game |website=[[CNN]] |publisher=[[WarnerMedia]] |date=July 30, 2004 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150527064255/http://edition.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/europe/07/30/uk.manhunt.storeban/ |archive-date=May 27, 2015 |url-status=live |access-date=November 8, 2012}}</ref> On August 2, 2004, it was reported that the Pakeerahs had hired Thompson to represent them in a £50 million [[wrongful death claim]] against [[Sony Interactive Entertainment|Sony Computer Entertainment]] (SCE) and Rockstar Games.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pinsentmasons.com/out-law/news/sony-to-be-sued-over-manhunt-murder |title=Sony to be sued over Manhunt murder |website=Out-Law |publisher=[[Pinsent Masons]] |date=August 2, 2004 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130314111918/http://www.out-law.com/page-4760 |archive-date=March 14, 2013 |url-status=live |access-date=January 16, 2020}}</ref> That day, the police officially denied any link between the game and the murder, citing drug-related robbery as the motive and revealing that the game had been found in Pakeerah's bedroom, not Leblanc's as originally reported.<ref name="reg">{{cite web |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/leicestershire/3538066.stm |title=Police reject game link to murder |website=BBC News | publisher=BBC |date=August 5, 2004 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120407073603/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/leicestershire/3538066.stm |archive-date=April 7, 2012 |url-status=live |access-date=January 17, 2020}}</ref><ref name="twist">{{cite web |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/new-twist-to-manhunt-murder-allegations |title=New twist to Manhunt murder allegations |author=Fahey, Rob |date=August 4, 2004 |website=GamesIndustry.biz |publisher=Gamer Network |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130419143344/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/new-twist-to-manhunt-murder-allegations |archive-date=April 19, 2013 |url-status=live |access-date=November 8, 2012}}</ref><ref name="BBCnolink">{{cite web |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/leicestershire/3624654.stm |title=Teenage murderer gets life term |website=BBC News |publisher=BBC |date=September 3, 2004 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111023045913/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/leicestershire/3624654.stm |archive-date=October 23, 2011 |url-status=live |access-date=January 17, 2020}}</ref> At the conclusion of the investigation, the police reaffirmed that they could not find sufficient evidence linking the game to the murder.<ref name="engadget 2007">{{Cite web|title=Jack Thompson at it again, wants Manhunt 2 pulled from UK|url=https://www.engadget.com/2007-02-26-jack-thompson-at-it-again-wants-manhunt-2-pulled-from-uk.html|access-date=July 30, 2020|website=Engadget|date=February 26, 2007 |language=en|author-first1=David|author-last1=Hinkle|archive-date=March 19, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319031642/https://www.engadget.com/p.gif?for=WaferFetch&beaconType=wafer_log&info=%7B%22duration%22%3A808%2C%22source%22%3A%22NETWORK_WITHOUT_CACHE%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22/_td/remote%3Fm_id%3Dengadget-article%26ctrl%3DArticleContainerV2%26module%3Darticle-container%26site%3Dengadget%26lang%3Den-US%26region%3DUS%26bucket%3Dengadget-def-bucket%26rid%3D0mhd671i1cvkl%26m_mode%3Djson%22%7D&rid=0mhd671i1cvkl&bucket=engadget-def-bucket&device=desktop&osName=windows%20nt&browserName=chrome&browserVersion=89.0|url-status=live}}</ref> The presiding judge placed sole responsibility with Leblanc after sentencing him to life.<ref name="BBCnolink" />

There was renewed controversy after the announcement of ''Manhunt 2'' in February 2007, with the Pakeerahs condemning its release.<ref>{{cite magazine |author=Ingram, Tim |date=February 8, 2007 |title=Murder victim's parents condemn Manhunt sequel |url=http://www.mcvuk.com/Murder-victims-parents-condemn-Manhunt-sequel |url-status=dead |magazine=[[MCV/Develop|The Market for Home Computing & Video Games]] |publisher=Intent Media |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070210061942/http://www.mcvuk.com/Murder-victims-parents-condemn-Manhunt-sequel |archive-date=February 10, 2007 |access-date=January 17, 2020}}</ref> Rockstar's parent company [[Take-Two Interactive]] issued a statement that "the Judge, defense, prosecution and Leicester police" in the case had refuted any connection to the game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/manhunt-2-excuses-in-early |title=Manhunt 2 excuses in early |author=Bramwell, Tom |date=February 8, 2007 |website=Eurogamer |publisher=Gamer Network |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130314110647/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/manhunt-2-excuses-in-early |archive-date=March 14, 2013 |url-status=live |access-date=November 27, 2012}}</ref> Jack Thompson unsuccessfully attempted to have ''Manhunt 2'' banned,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://gamepolitics.com/2007/04/19/breaking-grand-theft-auto-publisher-settles-lawsuit-against-jack-thompson |title=GTA Publisher, Jack Thompson Settle Lawsuit |website=[[GamePolitics.com]] |date=April 19, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120722105652/http://gamepolitics.com/2007/04/19/breaking-grand-theft-auto-publisher-settles-lawsuit-against-jack-thompson |archive-date=July 22, 2012 |url-status=dead |access-date=November 27, 2010}}</ref> claiming that Take-Two had lied about the incident and that police were incorrect in asserting the game had belonged to Pakeerah.<ref name="engadget 2007"/>

===Legal status===
In [[Video games in New Zealand|New Zealand]], the game was banned on December 11, 2003,<ref name="1up_nzban">{{cite web |url=http://www.1up.com/news/manhunt-banned-zealand |title=Manhunt Banned In New Zealand |website=1UP.com |publisher=Ziff Davis |year=2003 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150701115352/http://www.1up.com/news/manhunt-banned-zealand |archive-date=July 1, 2015 |url-status=dead |access-date=January 17, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.censorship.govt.nz/schools_manhunt.html |title=Banning of ''Manhunt'' |website=[[Office of Film and Literature Classification (New Zealand)|OFLC]] |date=December 17, 2003 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061001092528/http://www.censorship.govt.nz/schools_manhunt.html |archive-date=October 1, 2006 |url-status=dead |access-date=February 27, 2007}}</ref> with possession deemed an offence.<ref>[http://rangi.knowledge-basket.co.nz/gpacts/reprint/text/2005/se/042se131.html Films, Videos, and Publications Classification Act 1993, 131]{{dead link|date=May 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> [[Bill Hastings (censor)|Bill Hastings]], the Chief Censor, stated "it's a game where the only thing you do is kill everybody you see ... You have to at least acquiesce in these murders and possibly tolerate, or even move towards enjoying them, which is injurious to the public good."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/manhunt-banned-in-new-zealand/1100-6085503/ |title=Manhunt banned in New Zealand |author=Thorsen, Tor |date=December 12, 2003 |website=GameSpot |publisher=CBS Interactive |access-date=January 17, 2020 |archive-date=February 14, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190214213316/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/manhunt-banned-in-new-zealand/1100-6085503/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2023, the Office reconsidered ''Manhunt'' and classified it R18.<ref>{{cite web|title=OFLC No. 2200483.000 Register Page|publisher=NZ Register of Classification Decisions|url=https://register.classificationoffice.govt.nz/Pages/Screens/DDA/PublicationDecisionInformationPage.aspx|date=2023-01-19|access-date=2023-12-26}}</ref>

In Australia, the game was initially allowed under a MA15+ classification, but this decision was reversed by the [[Australian Classification Board]] in September 2004, after an appeal by the [[Attorney-General of Australia|Attorney-General]] [[Philip Ruddock]]. As a consequence, the game was effectively banned, mandating a recall of all copies still being sold in stores.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theregister.co.uk/2004/09/30/oz_manhunt_ban/ |title=Australia bans Manhunt |author=Smith, Tony |date=September 30, 2004 |website=[[The Register]] |publisher=Situation Publishing |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111104212117/http://www.theregister.co.uk/2004/09/30/oz_manhunt_ban/ |archive-date=November 4, 2011 |url-status=live |access-date=February 27, 2007}}</ref> Before its recall, ''Manhunt'' had already sold 18,000 units in Australia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/technology/ban-increases-call-for-r18-rating-20041014-gdjwy8.html|title=Ban increases call for R18+ rating|work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]|publisher=[[Nine Entertainment Co.]]|date=October 14, 2004|access-date=August 15, 2020|archive-date=October 26, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201026194636/https://www.smh.com.au/technology/ban-increases-call-for-r18-rating-20041014-gdjwy8.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

In Canada, following a meeting in Toronto on December 22, 2003, between Hastings and officials from the Ontario Ministry of Consumer and Business Services, ''Manhunt'' became the first video game in Ontario to be classified as a film and was restricted to adults on February 3, 2004. Apart from Ontario, however, ''Manhunt'' had little or no classification problems elsewhere in North America. The [[British Columbia Film Classification Office]] reviewed the game after the controversy in Ontario and deemed the Mature rating by the [[Entertainment Software Rating Board|ESRB]] to be appropriate.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bcfilmclass.com/decisions/2004/manhunt.pdf |title=Opinion Review: In the Matter of Manhunt published by Rockstar Games |date=February 6, 2004 |website=[[British Columbia Film Classification Office]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060214090109/http://bcfilmclass.com/decisions/2004/manhunt.pdf |archive-date=February 14, 2006 |url-status=dead |access-date=October 12, 2006}}</ref>

In Germany, the [[Amtsgericht]] in Munich confiscated the PlayStation 2 version of ''Manhunt'' on July 19, 2004, for violation of [[Strafgesetzbuch#§ 131: Representation of violence|§ 131 StGB]] ("representation of violence"). According to the court, the game portrays the killing of humans as fun. They also said it glorified [[vigilantism]], which they considered harmful.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wurm |first=Gerald |title=Beschlagnahme - Manhunt (Schnittberichte.com) |url=https://www.schnittberichte.com/svds.php?Page=IndexDocs&ID=3555&idid=828 |access-date=2023-06-16 |website=www.schnittberichte.com |language=de}}</ref> All other versions got indexed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wurm |first=Gerald |title=Indizierung - Manhunt (Schnittberichte.com) |url=https://www.schnittberichte.com/svds.php?Page=IndexDocs&ID=3555&idid=630 |access-date=2023-06-16 |website=www.schnittberichte.com |language=de}}</ref>

In Thailand, the government tagged ''Manhunt'' a violent video game in August 2008, following [[Murder of Khuan Phokaeng|the murder of a taxi driver]] in [[Bangkok]] who was killed by an 18-year-old man obsessed with ''GTA IV''. As a result, the government banned the sale of ''GTA'' and labeled numerous other games, including ''Manhunt''.<ref name="nbcnews">{{cite news |last1=Ahuja |first1=Ambika |title=Thailand tags 10 games violent after murder |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna26095324 |access-date=31 May 2026 |work=[[NBC News]] |date=8 August 2008 |archive-date=27 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230127091935/https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna26095324 |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Steam release crack protection issues ===
To combat [[Video game piracy|piracy]], the retail version contained two layers of [[digital rights management]] (DRM): the [[SecuROM]] system and several game-breaking mechanisms that are activated when SecuROM is missing. To ship the game to Steam without third party DRM, Rockstar Games re-released it with an existing crack by [[Razor 1911]]. As this was uncovered in 2010, the company quickly released a new version of the retail release with only SecuROM removed. The proprietary measures were not addressed, leading to a broken version being sold on Steam. Prior to 2023, the crack protection mechanisms, such as gates and doors not working properly blocking progress through the game, were interpreted as issues with compatibility on newer operating systems. However, it was discovered the Steam release had crack protection measures active despite being an official release due to the incomplete removal of the DRM.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/after-15-years-gta-devs-anti-piracy-measures-are-still-only-hurting-legitimate-players/|title=After 15 years, GTA dev's anti-piracy measures are still only hurting legitimate players|first=Dustin|last=Bailey|work=[[PCGamesN]]|date=September 5, 2023|access-date=September 5, 2023}}</ref>

==Legacy==
{{See also|Manhunt 2}}
''Manhunt'' has garnered a [[cult following]] among fans,<ref name="PSN"/> and was cited by a ''[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]'' article in March 2016 as one of Rockstar's "very best" games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/why-i-adore-manhunt-the-quintessential-video-game-nasty-210/|title=Why I Adore the Legendarily Crass, Violent Video Game 'Manhunt'|work=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]|publisher=[[Vice Media]]|first=Ed|last=Smith|date=March 28, 2016|access-date=August 15, 2020|archive-date=May 5, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190505155922/https://www.vice.com/en_us/article/mvxzyn/why-i-adore-manhunt-the-quintessential-video-game-nasty-210|url-status=live}}</ref> Likewise, ''[[Game Informer]]'' considered the game a "dark, underappreciated masterpiece".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2016/03/25/manhunt-is-a-dark-underappreciated-masterpiece.aspx|title=Opinion — Manhunt Is The Dark, Underappreciated Masterpiece We Deserve|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|publisher=[[GameStop]]|first=Javy|last=Gwaltney|date=March 25, 2016|access-date=August 30, 2020|archive-date=August 13, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200813182522/https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2016/03/25/manhunt-is-a-dark-underappreciated-masterpiece.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref> It was recognised as an example of the "best of gaming horror" by ''[[VentureBeat]]'' in October 2011,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/community/2011/10/24/the-best-of-gaming-horror-part-v-manhunt/|title=The Best of Gaming Horror Part V - Manhunt|publisher=[[VentureBeat]]|first=Stan|last=Rezaee|date=October 24, 2011|access-date=August 15, 2020|archive-date=October 20, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020203347/https://venturebeat.com/community/2011/10/24/the-best-of-gaming-horror-part-v-manhunt/|url-status=live}}</ref> included in the ''[[1001 Video Games You Must Play Before You Die]]'' in 2010,<ref>{{cite book |title=1001 Video Games You Must Play Before You Die |author=Mott, Tony |year=2010 |publisher=Quintessence Editions Ltd. |location=London |isbn=978-1-74173-076-0 |page=546}}</ref> and listed at #85 in ''IGN''{{'}}s "Top 100 PlayStation 2 Games" that same year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/lists/ps2-games/85 |title=Top 100 PlayStation 2 Games (Manhunt - #85) |website=IGN |publisher=Ziff Davis |access-date=January 16, 2020 |archive-date=June 30, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190630104323/https://www.ign.com/lists/ps2-games/85 |url-status=live }}</ref>

A sequel, ''[[Manhunt 2]]'', was released in October 2007 in the United States and October 2008 in Europe.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2007/08/manhunt-2-will-see-halloween-release-date-after-getting-m-rating/|title=Manhunt 2 will see Halloween release date after getting M rating|work=[[Ars Technica]]|publisher=[[Condé Nast]]|first=Eric|last=Bangeman|date=August 24, 2007|access-date=August 15, 2020|archive-date=December 13, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131213164116/http://arstechnica.com/gaming/2007/08/manhunt-2-will-see-halloween-release-date-after-getting-m-rating/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2008/10/03/manhunt-2-dated-in-uk|title=Manhunt 2 Dated in UK|first=Matt|last=Wales|date=October 3, 2008|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=[[Ziff Davis]]|access-date=August 15, 2020|archive-date=October 21, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021025003/https://www.ign.com/articles/2008/10/03/manhunt-2-dated-in-uk|url-status=live}}</ref> Although the sequel retains many of the stealth elements used in its predecessor, ''Manhunt 2''{{'}}s storyline is completely unrelated to the first game.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.gamespot.com/wii/action/manhunt2/news.html?sid=6172967 |title= ''Manhunt 2'' Hands-on Preview |website= [[GameSpot]] |date= June 21, 2007 |access-date= November 26, 2012 |archive-date= March 19, 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230319031649/https://www.gamespot.com/games/manhunt-2/news/ |url-status= live }}</ref>

WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: MediEvil (2019 video game)
======================================================================

{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2021}}
{{short description|2019 video game}}
{{Infobox video game

| image      = MediEvil Box art cropped.png

| publisher  = [[Sony Interactive Entertainment]]
| director   =

'''''MediEvil''''' is a 2019 [[action-adventure game]] developed by [[Other Ocean Interactive|Other Ocean Emeryville]] and published by [[Sony Interactive Entertainment]] for the [[PlayStation 4]]. The player controls the protagonist, Sir Daniel Fortesque, through a series of levels, utilizing various weapons to attack enemies as well as encountering several [[Non-player character|non-playable characters]]. It is a remake of ''[[MediEvil]]'', which was originally developed by British video game developer [[Guerrilla Cambridge|SCE Cambridge Studio]] and released for the [[PlayStation (console)|PlayStation]] in 1998. 

The ''MediEvil'' remake was first announced as a remaster of ''MediEvil'' in late 2017 and later as a remake the following year. The developers of ''MediEvil'' took advantage of the advances in technology since the first ''MediEvil'' to enhance aspects, while trying to avoid straying too far from the presentation of the original. Additional features not present in the original were included in the remake. The ''MediEvil'' remake was released on October 25, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Martin |first=Liam |date=November 1, 2018 |title=MediEvil PS4 Remaster release date REVEALED with NEW PlayStation 4 gameplay |url=https://www.express.co.uk/entertainment/gaming/1038935/MediEvil-PS4-Remake-gameplay-Sony-PlayStation-release-date |website=Express}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2019/5/9/18563526/medievil-ps4-remake-release-date-gameplay-trailer|title=MediEvil remake comes to PS4 this October|last=McWhertor|first=Michael|publisher=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=May 9, 2019|accessdate=May 10, 2019}}</ref> Various bonus content was included in special editions. 

''MediEvil'' received mixed reviews from critics, who praised its presentation, but criticized some aspects of its gameplay. The game is dedicated to Zarok's voice actor, [[Paul Darrow]], who died on June 3, 2019.

==Gameplay==
{{see also|MediEvil#Gameplay|l1=Gameplay in MediEvil}}
[[File:MediEvil remake.png|thumb|left|Sir Daniel Fortesque encountering a Rhinotaur in the "Crystal Caves" level. The optional "Dan Cam" camera viewpoint is being used.]]
''MediEvil'' takes place across a series of levels selectable from a map of Gallowmere.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.destructoid.com/review-medievil-ps4--569800.phtml|title=Review: MediEvil (PS4)|last=Carter|first=Chris|date=October 23, 2019|website=Destructoid|access-date=October 23, 2019}}</ref> The character, Sir Daniel Fortesque, is able to utilize a variety of weapons ranging from close range weapons such as swords and clubs to long range weapons such as throwing daggers and bows, many of which can be charged for a more powerful attack.<ref name=":3">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YHx1KOBCM-A |title=MediEvil - A Bonehead's Guide to Gallowmere: Maximizing One's Offense {{!}} PS4 |date=October 17, 2019 |publisher=PlayStation |access-date=July 25, 2020 |website=YouTube }}</ref> When not in possession of any weapons, Sir Daniel is able to use his arm for melee and ranged attacks.<ref name=":3" /> Sir Daniel is also able to equip a shield alongside his weapons for defense, though they can only resist a limited amount of damage and do not protect Dan from certain types of damage, such as long falls.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R4ow7TTngNs |title=MediEvil - Using One's Shield {{!}} PS4 |date=October 3, 2019 |publisher=PlayStation |access-date=July 25, 2020 |website=YouTube }}</ref> As Sir Daniel is hit by enemies, he will lose part of his [[Health (game terminology)|health bar]]. If his entire health bar is depleted, the game will end. While Sir Daniel does not recover health automatically between levels, he can utilize Life Bottles to refill all of his health should it be completely depleted.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.destructoid.com/medievil-guide-life-is-the-most-precious-resource-so-bank-it-570162.phtml|title=MediEvil guide: Life is the most precious resource, so bank it|last=Carter|first=Chris|date=October 23, 2019|website=Destructoid|access-date=October 25, 2019}}</ref>

Sir Dan is able to encounter two varieties of gargoyle heads throughout the game: green gargoyles offer Sir Dan information, while blue gargoyles offer him ammunition for his weapons in exchange for gold.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.pushsquare.com/news/2019/10/guide_medievil_ps4_-_tips_and_tricks_for_beginners|title=Guide: MediEvil PS4 - Tips and Tricks for Beginners|last=Tailby|first=Stephen|date=October 24, 2019|website=Push Square|access-date=October 28, 2019}}</ref> In each level, Sir Dan is able to find a chalice of Souls, which can be collected if the player has defeated enough enemies. Dan can use the chalices to gain access to the Hall of Heroes, where he can talk to one of several non-playable characters to receive a new weapon or other item.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2019-10-24-medievil-review-polished-remake-fails-to-de-clunk-the-ps1-original|title=MediEvil review - polished remake fails to de-clunk the PS1 original|last=Blake|first=Vikki|date=October 24, 2019|work=Eurogamer|access-date=October 24, 2019}}</ref> If Sir Dan collects all chalices, the true ending will be shown.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pushsquare.com/news/2019/10/guide_medievil_ps4_-_how_to_get_the_good_ending_in_medievil|title=Guide: MediEvil PS4 - How to Get the Good Ending in MediEvil|last=Tailby|first=Stephen|date=October 22, 2019|website=Push Square|access-date=October 25, 2019}}</ref>

While the game remains largely identical in content to the original ''MediEvil'', several new features have been introduced. This includes the ability to toggle between a primary and secondary weapon, first introduced as a feature in ''[[MediEvil 2]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pushsquare.com/news/2019/11/guide_medievil_ps4_-_tips_and_tricks_for_beginners|title=Guide: MediEvil PS4 - Tips and Tricks for Beginners|last=Tailby|first=Stephen|date=November 12, 2019|website=Push Square|access-date=January 6, 2020}}</ref> the "Dan Cam", an optional camera viewpoint which uses an over-the-shoulder perspective,<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IBrWVHq9q68 |title=MediEvil - Changing One's Perspective {{!}} PS4 |date=October 10, 2019 |publisher=PlayStation |access-date=July 25, 2020 |website=YouTube }}</ref> and a compendium of information about the characters and enemies, known as the Book of Gallowmere.<ref name=":2" /> Optional "Lost Souls" objectives have also been incorporated into the game, which require Sir Dan to complete a mission received from a ghost found in each level.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pushsquare.com/reviews/ps4/medievil|title=MediEvil Review (PS4)|last=Tailby|first=Stephen|date=October 23, 2019|website=Push Square|access-date=October 23, 2019}}</ref> If all Lost Souls objectives are completed, the player unlocks the option to play the original ''MediEvil'' on the menu screen, under the name of "Old Game".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pushsquare.com/news/2019/11/guide_medievil_ps4_-_how_to_unlock_the_original_ps1_game_in_the_remake|title=Guide: MediEvil PS4 - How to Unlock the Original PS1 Game in the Remake|last=Tailby|first=Stephen|date=October 31, 2019|website=Push Square|access-date=January 10, 2020}}</ref>

==Development==
According to the executive producer of the ''MediEvil'' remake, Jeff Nachbauer, Other Ocean Emeryville wished to keep most elements from the original ''MediEvil'' intact, unless they felt there was a good reason to change something. This included the retention of several glitches present in the original ''MediEvil'', which were considered by the developers to be crucial to the feel of the game. One of these glitches was for sword swings that made the motion irregular and unpredictable.<ref name=":5" /> The developers researched music the original developers would have listened to at the time of the development of the first ''MediEvil''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blog.us.playstation.com/2019/08/14/behind-the-scenes-of-medievils-upcoming-ps4-resurrection/|title=Behind the Scenes of MediEvil's Upcoming PS4 Resurrection|last=Accordino|first=Nick|date=August 14, 2019|website=PlayStation Blog|access-date=October 4, 2019}}</ref> Level geometry was extracted from the original ''MediEvil'' and imported into the remake's engine to serve as a reference for the placement of level elements. Due to the game's further [[draw distance]] and wider aspect ratio, new background areas that did not exist in the original ''MediEvil'' needed to be created, and additional trees and foliage were added to certain areas.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blog.us.playstation.com/2018/12/13/remaking-fan-favorites-how-devs-resurrected-crash-medievil-resident-evil-2-and-spyro-for-ps4/?ref-tag=249442|title=Remaking Fan Favorites: How Devs Resurrected Crash, MediEvil, Resident Evil 2, and Spyro for PS4|last=Shuman|first=Sid|date=December 13, 2018|website=PlayStation Blog|access-date=October 4, 2019}}</ref> Enemy behaviors left in the [[source code]] of the original ''MediEvil'', but removed from the finished game due to time constraints, were restored for the ''MediEvil'' remake.<ref name=":5" /> 

=== Character design ===
Art director [[Nick Bruty]] believed that it was crucial to keep the feel of the first ''MediEvil'' in Sir Daniel Fortesque's design, while still adding extra detail and shape to the low-resolution 3D model from the original game. Sir Dan's arms were made longer, as they were considered to look strange in the higher resolution of the ''MediEvil'' remake. Sir Dan's armor was redesigned to be more grounded while still accommodating for his animations. They had initially given Dan's armor a cleaner design, but made his armor more tattered later in development. The design of Sir Dan's skull went through several iterations, with the finalized design intending to strike a balance between the more gritty design of the original ''MediEvil'' and the more humorous design of ''[[MediEvil: Resurrection]]''. Due to advances in technology since the development of the first ''MediEvil'', Other Ocean was able to create a wider range of expressions for Sir Dan compared to the original game.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|url=https://blog.us.playstation.com/2019/12/20/medievils-short-lived-demo-returns-today-with-new-content/|title=MediEvil's Short-Lived Demo Returns Today With New Content|last=Accordino|first=Nick|date=December 20, 2019|website=PlayStation Blog|access-date=January 7, 2020}}</ref>

=== Voice acting ===
Most in-game dialogue was recycled from the original ''MediEvil'' (the only exception to this is Zarok's command of "Fire!" in the cinematic showing what had really happened to Dan). Jason Wilson, the voice actor of Sir Dan in ''MediEvil'' and ''MediEvil: Resurrection'', reprised his role. Unlike the original ''MediEvil'', where Sir Dan's muffled voice effect was created by recording his lines while wearing a bucket, the effect was instead post-processed for the ''MediEvil'' remake.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=https://www.escapistmagazine.com/v2/medievil-remake-devs-on-being-faithful-without-feeling-like-a-bad-cover-band/|title=MediEvil Remake Devs on Being Faithful 'Without Feeling Like a Bad Cover Band'|last=Lee|first=Patrick|date=October 21, 2019|website=Escapist Magazine|access-date=October 28, 2019}}</ref> Tom Baker was replaced as the voice of the narrator by [[Lani Minella]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/medievil-remake-feels-like-dark-souls-says-playstation/|title=MediEvil remake "feels like Dark Souls", says PlayStation|last=Blake|first=Vikki|date=August 25, 2019|website=GamesRadar|access-date=October 8, 2019}}</ref>

=== Music ===
Andrew Barnabas and Paul Arnold, who had composed the soundtrack for the previous three games in the series, returned to compose for the ''MediEvil'' remake. The music of the ''MediEvil'' remake was orchestrated by [[Prague Symphony Orchestra]].<ref name=":4" /> The soundtrack consists of remastered versions of music that appeared in ''MediEvil: Resurrection'', orchestral arrangements of tracks from the original ''MediEvil'', and new tracks composed exclusively for the ''MediEvil'' remake.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wshu.org/post/bob-and-barns-fresh-music-medievil-re-release|title=Bob And Barn's Fresh Music For 'MediEvil' Re-Release|last=Remington|first=Kate|date=November 15, 2019|work=WSHU|access-date=November 16, 2019}}</ref>

=== Emulator ===
A software PlayStation emulator was developed so that the original game could be unlocked and played on the PlayStation 4, which at the time lacked any backwards compatibility with PlayStation 1 games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yin-Poole |first=Wesley |date=20 July 2020 |title=Modder discovers PS1 emulator hidden inside MediEvil PS4 |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/modder-discovers-ps1-emulator-hidden-inside-medievil-ps4 |access-date=17 November 2022 |website=Eurogamer.net |language=en-gb}}</ref> The inclusion of the software led to attention from the modding community after launch, and resulted in attempts to run other games through ''MediEvil'''s PlayStation emulator.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lennox |first=Jesse |date=20 July 2020 |title=Fully-Functional PS1 Emulator Found Inside The MediEvil Remake |url=https://www.thegamer.com/medievil-remake-ps1-emulator/ |access-date=17 November 2022 |website=TheGamer |language=en-US}}</ref> Formal support for emulating other original PlayStation games on PS4 did not emerge until the 2022 revamp of [[PlayStation Plus]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robinson |first=Andy |date=16 May 2022 |title=Sony has revealed some of PS Plus's new classic, PS4 and PS5 games |url=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/sony-has-revealed-some-of-ps-pluss-classic-ps4-and-ps5-games/ |access-date=17 November 2022 |website=Video Games Chronicle |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Release==
The ''MediEvil'' remake was first announced as a remaster of ''MediEvil'' at the 2017 [[PlayStation Experience]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sanchez |first=Miranda |date=December 9, 2017 |title=PSX 2017: MediEvil PS4 Remaster Announced |url=https://ca.ign.com/articles/2017/12/09/psx-2017-medievil-ps4-remaster-announced |access-date=September 25, 2019 |website=IGN}}</ref> ''MediEvil'' was fully revealed on October 31, 2018,<ref>{{Cite web |last=McWhertor |first=Michael |date=October 31, 2018 |title=Watch the first trailer for MediEvil for PlayStation 4 |url=https://www.polygon.com/2018/10/31/18044066/medievil-ps4-trailer-remake |access-date=July 25, 2020 |website=Polygon}}</ref> and was confirmed to be a full remake, instead of a remaster as was previously announced. In the May 9, 2019, PlayStation State of Play, the digital only "Digital Deluxe Edition" version was revealed, which includes the Super Armor from ''[[MediEvil 2]]'' (that now increases the gold Sir Dan earns), a theme based on the game for the [[PlayStation 4 system software|PlayStation 4 user interface]], a digital art book, a digital graphic novel prequel known as ''MediEvil: Fate's Arrow,''<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1162379594101641216 |user=GunnComics |title='MediEvil: Fate's Arrow.' @Trepan (Chris Sorrell) and I are delighted to announce that our prequel/sequel story to the original MediEvil will be released as a hardback book by @ComicsTitan with @playstation this Halloween! Here's a peak at the art. #medievil |author=Jay Gunn |date=August 16, 2019 |access-date=July 25, 2020 |url=https://twitter.com/gunncomics/status/1162379594101641216}}</ref> and a digital music player featuring the soundtrack, the latter receiving a future update allowing the user to download the music.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Devore |first=Jordan |date=May 9, 2019 |title=Relive the glory of MediEvil on PS4 this October |url=https://www.destructoid.com/relive-the-glory-of-medievil-on-ps4-this-october-553105.phtml |access-date=July 25, 2020 |website=Destructoid}}</ref> In the September 24, 2019, PlayStation State of Play, a demo of ''MediEvil'', known as ''MediEvil: Short-Lived Demo'', was announced to be available from the end of the presentation until October 6, 2019. The demo features an unlockable helmet item that can carry over to the full game. The helmet is based on the Japanese version of the original ''MediEvil'', which features Sir Dan wearing a helmet by default, and also increases the difficulty level.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/medievil-demo-hacks-onto-the-playstation-store/|title=MediEvil demo hacks its way onto the PlayStation Store|last=Gerblick|first=Jordan|date=September 24, 2019|website=Gamesradar|access-date=October 4, 2019}}</ref> A version of the ''Short-Lived Demo'' with additional levels was released on December 20, 2019.<ref name=":6" />

== Reception ==

| VG = 7/10<ref name="VG">{{cite web |last=Walker |first=Rich |date=October 23, 2019 |url=https://www.videogamer.com/reviews/medievil-review |title=MediEvil review |publisher=VideoGamer.com |accessdate=October 23, 2019}}</ref>
}}

''MediEvil'' received mixed reviews from critics. It received an aggregate score of 67% from [[GameRankings]]<ref name=GR/> and a score of 67 from review aggregator [[Metacritic]] based on 72 critics, indicating mixed or average reviews.<ref name="MC"/>

Praise was directed at the visual design, which was considered to be faithful to the original ''MediEvil'',<ref name="GI" /><ref name="GRadar" /> and the character, setting, and story.<ref name="GI" /><ref name="GSpot" /><ref name="GRadar" /><ref name="IGN" /> Aspects of ''MediEvil''{{'}}s gameplay design were often considered by critics to feel outdated, in particular the lack of a checkpoint mechanic.<ref name="IGN" /><ref name="GI"/><ref name="GSpot"/> Some mechanics like the instant death upon falling into water were also subject to criticism,<ref name=":1" /><ref name="GI" /> and were considered to be aggravated by the unreliable controls and cameras.<ref name="Destruct"/><ref name="GSpot" /> Combat was criticized for being frustrating and imprecise.<ref name="IGN" /><ref name="GRadar" />

''[[IGN]]''{{'}}s Travis Northup considered ''MediEvil''{{'}}s "relentlessly charming story" as its greatest strength, and praised the added details and personality to the visuals and audio, but described the combat as "sloppy and disorienting".<ref name="IGN" /> ''[[GameSpot]]''{{'}}s James Swinbanks, while also praising characters and visual style, shared similar concerns about the combat as well as other basic tasks which are made difficult by the sloppy controls and camera movements.<ref name="GSpot" /> ''Destructoid''{{'}}s Chris Carter felt that people who did not like the original ''MediEvil'' would not like the remake either, and thought the combat mechanics "might be a little too retro for modern audiences", comparing them to older hack-and-slash games such as ''[[Golden Axe (video game)|Golden Axe]]''.<ref name=":1" /> ''[[Game Informer]]''{{'}}s Andrew Reiner thought that ''MediEvil''{{'}}s combat system felt imprecise, and compared the game unfavorably to other remakes such as ''[[Crash Bandicoot N. Sane Trilogy]]'' and ''[[Spyro Reignited Trilogy]]''.<ref name="GI" /> In line with other reviews, ''[[GamesRadar+]]'' and VideoGamer.com praised the visuals, but criticized the outdated game design.<ref name="GRadar" /><ref name="VG" />

=== Sales ===
In the United Kingdom, ''MediEvil'' was the fifth-best-selling game in its week of release.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.pushsquare.com/news/2019/10/uk_sales_charts_wwe_2k20_debuts_in_third_despite_its_countless_glitches_going_viral|title=UK Sales Charts: WWE 2K20 Debuts in Third Despite Its Countless Glitches Going Viral|last=Tailby|first=Stephen|date=October 28, 2019|work=Push Square|access-date=November 21, 2019}}</ref> On November 5, 2019, ''MediEvil'' was listed as the third-best-selling game of the week in a chart in the combined download and retail encompassing 43 countries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Batchelor |first=James |date=November 5, 2019 |title=Call of Duty: Modern Warfare dominates the EMEAA charts |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2019-11-05-call-of-duty-modern-warfare-dominates-the-emeaa-charts |access-date=July 26, 2020 |website=GamesIndustry.biz |language=en}}</ref>
